Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
items.abstract: Abstract Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2 . How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
items.abstract: Abstract CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2 . Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6 . Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST ( Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8 . However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9 . Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide 1–4 , yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
items.abstract: Abstract Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2 , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7 . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8 . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8 . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

Cardiomyocyte-derived circulating extracellular vesicles enable a non-invasive liquid biopsy of human myocardium
items.last_author_affiliation: Cardiovascular Research Center, Massachusetts General Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. Electronic address: sdas@mgh.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Non-invasive interrogation of difficult-to-sample tissues remains a central challenge in human health. Here, we identify and characterize cardiomyocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs; "cardiovesicles") as a liquid interface to the myocardium. Integrating induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, genetic models, and multi-omics, we identify two cardiomyocyte-enriched surface markers (POPDC2 and CHRNE), enabling antibody-based cardiovesicle immunocapture from human plasma. Cardiovesicles are enriched for cardiomyocyte transcripts, exhibiting disease-specific transcriptional signatures in heart failure and myocardial infarction. Paired human myocardial tissue-plasma analyses demonstrate cardiac enrichment (versus bulk EVs) and concordance with myocardial single-nucleus transcriptional profiles. In patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass, cardiovesicles capture rapid, dynamic transcriptional changes that parallel cardiomyocyte (not fibroblast, endothelial, and myeloid) responses to ischemic stress. Functional genomics implicates cardiovesicle transcripts in cardiomyocyte cell-specific cardiovascular disease liability in large human populations. Cardiovesicles may capture dynamic cardiomyocyte states in humans that reflect genetic disease liability, supporting an EV-based approach to non-invasive liquid biopsy of the myocardium.

A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
items.abstract: Abstract Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B . thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

items.title: An explainable deep-learning framework for predicting multisystem outcomes in comorbidity-free MASLD
items.abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with hepatic and extrahepatic morbidity, but non-invasive tests provide indirect, largely cross-sectional risk estimates, limiting continuous and individualised prognostication. Here we develop AEGIS-MASLD, an explainable deep learning framework integrating dual-stain liver biopsy images, clinical data and longitudinal lifestyle records to predict 13 MASLD-related multisystem outcomes. This retrospective multicentre study included 814 adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD without baseline comorbidities, followed for a median of 203 months. The model was developed in 546 patients from three Chinese centres using five-fold cross-validation and externally validated in 268 patients from six independent centres. In external validation, the model predicted 12 non-fatal outcomes with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.766–0.867, outperforming conventional histological and non-invasive fibrosis scores. All-cause mortality was evaluated separately using pathology and laboratory data. Annual risk estimates for non-fatal outcomes were updated as lifestyle exposures changed. Tissue analyses identified 24 histopathological phenotype clusters, linking fibrotic clusters to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and inflammatory clusters to cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that digital pathology analysis of routinely obtained biopsy material, combined with clinical and lifestyle data, could support individualised multisystem risk assessment and follow-up in patients with MASLD undergoing biopsy-based evaluation.

items.title: Evolutionary Neuroskeletal Biology
Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
items.abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

items.title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
items.abstract: Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

items.title: Directional atomic-ordering gradients enable fatigue-resistant superelasticity in carbon tube aerogels
items.abstract: Abstract Elastic inorganic aerogels are highly attractive for weight-sensitive applications in extreme environments, yet integrating high strength, large-strain recoverability and fatigue resistance within a single architecture remains a longstanding challenge. Here we show that directional atomic-ordering gradients in carbon tube aerogels provide a structural route to overcoming this trade-off. Guided by finite-element analysis, we create atomic-ordering gradient junctions through stepwise-modulated chemical vapor deposition, producing a radial increase in carbon ordering across load-bearing tube walls and inter-tube junctions. Multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the directional gradient enables the outer crystalline region to function as a sliding-enabled stress-relief layer, thereby promoting stress delocalization, suppressing bond rupture and reducing irreversible energy dissipation before network densification becomes dominant. As a result, the directional-gradient aerogel sustains reversible compression up to 95% strain, reaches a maximum stress of 8.0 MPa, and retains ~87% of its initial maximum stress after 10,000 cycles at 90% strain with only ~6% permanent deformation. These findings show that controlling atomic ordering at carbon tube junctions offers an effective way to improve the mechanical robustness and fatigue resistance of highly compressible porous solids.

items.title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere

Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
items.abstract: Abstract Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

items.title: Chip-scale narrow-linewidth optical parametric oscillators
items.abstract: Abstract Continuous-wave-pumped optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide an exciting avenue to generate coherent radiation at wavelength regions that are difficult to reach by traditional semiconductor optical amplifiers. However, attaining ultra-narrow linewidth operation in OPOs requires pump lasers with exceptional purity to begin with. Here, we demonstrate an integrated Kerr nonlinear OPO featuring an integrated external cavity based on ultralow-loss silicon nitride that results in a continuous-wave signal with a 15-fold intrinsic linewidth reduction compared to the pump, down to 10 Hz. Our numerical analysis indicates that the intrinsic linewidth can be reduced below the Schawlow-Townes limit of a single-cavity OPO depending on the feedback length and strength of the external cavity. Utilizing an integrated erbium-doped waveguide amplifier, we further demonstrate sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth coherent oscillation. These results establish an effective pathway towards chip-scale ultra-coherent light sources with high power and broad wavelength tunability, opening new opportunities for high-precision optical sensing and detection.

items.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
items.abstract: Abstract Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

items.title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
items.abstract: Abstract Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

items.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
authors: On behalf of the German Diabetes Study (GDS) group
Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank Study Group
items.last_author: Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank Study Group
items.abstract: Abstract Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort ( N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) ( N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, P log-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, p log-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c ( p AUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant ( p = 0.035) and age-related ( p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

items.title: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
items.abstract: Abstract Osteoclasts are essential for bone remodeling and homeostasis. Their excessive activation drives pathological bone loss disorders such as periodontitis and arthritis. Current osteoclast-inhibiting therapies are limited by adverse effects and poor specificity, underscoring the importance to identify new regulators of osteoclastogenesis. Here, we conducted a pooled CRISPR–Cas9 screen targeting cluster of differentiation (CD) genes to uncover novel modulators of osteoclast differentiation and identified CD300LD, a single-pass transmembrane protein, as a potent driver of osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deletion impaired osteoclastogenesis in cell line and primary bone-marrow–derived macrophages. In vivo, myeloid-specific Cd300ld knockout mice exhibited significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and osteoclast numbers in experimental periodontitis, as well as attenuated joint inflammation and bone erosion in arthritis models, whereas bone remodeling during skeletal development remained unaltered. Mechanistically, cholesterol acts as extracellular activator for CD300LD to activate osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deficiency intracellularly inhibited phosphorylation of FES, SYK, and STAT3. Consistently, loss of Fes , Syk or Stat3 recapitulated the Cd300ld -deficient phenotypes, establishing a CD300LD–FES–SYK–STAT3 signaling axis essential for osteoclast differentiation. Together, these findings identify CD300LD as a critical, previously unrecognized driver of osteoclastogenesis and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory bone loss.

items.title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
items.abstract: Abstract Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

items.title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
items.abstract: Abstract The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp 2 -hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

items.title: Scalable 3D hybrid integrated photonic computing chiplets
A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
items.abstract: Abstract Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

items.title: Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures
Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice

Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
items.abstract: Abstract Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.
