Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron-OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl-amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation-decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl-amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models.

items.title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design.
items.last_author_affiliation: Infection, Immunity and Inflammation, Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health, University College London, London, UK. d.goldblatt@ucl.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

items.title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Engineering and Low-Carbon Technology, College of Chemical and Biological Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, 310058, China.
items.abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS2-based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is -58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS2-based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

items.title: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine, David Geffen School of Medicine, University of California, Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA, USA. jocelynkim@mednet.ucla.edu.
items.abstract: Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound.

items.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability.
items.last_author_affiliation: Program in Cancer and Stem Cell Biology, Duke-NUS Medical School, Singapore, Singapore. hongwen.tang@duke-nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Here, we identify ifc, the Drosophila orthologue of DEGS1, as a key regulator of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). Ifc/DEGS1 encodes a sphingolipid desaturase that converts dihydroceramide to ceramide during ceramide biosynthesis. In Drosophila, ifc overexpression expands MuSC populations and suppresses differentiation, mirroring RMS like properties. Consistently, DEGS1 is upregulated in RMS cells, where it drives lipid droplet biogenesis and activates mTORC1 signaling to inhibit lipophagy, leading to aberrant lipid droplet accumulation. This metabolic rewiring positions lipid droplets, which have been largely overlooked in RMS biology, as central hubs that promote proliferation, suppress differentiation, and enhance metastatic potential, thereby driving RMS progression. Importantly, dual pharmacologic inhibition of DEGS1 and mTORC1 synergistically suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, revealing a lipid droplet-dependent vulnerability in RMS. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS.

items.title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Marine Biogeochemistry Division, GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel, Kiel, Germany.
items.abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m-2 day-1 per decade (p < 0.05). This decline is driven by reduced spring nitrate availability, resulting from slower winter nitrate replenishment rates, increased upstream consumption, and net nitrate export linked to Atlantification. Moreover, a North Atlantic-Arctic atmospheric wave train and reduced freshwater input have deepened the mixed layer, lowering light availability and further limiting production. These findings indicate that continued warming will likely suppress spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone, triggering nutrient-driven cascading effects on Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

items.title: One Health in action: regional innovations and shared challenges in addressing antimicrobial resistance.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Global Health Network, Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. trudie.lang@ndm.ox.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries, yet perspectives and innovations from these regions remain underrepresented. During World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2025, the AMR Knowledge Hub convened a four-day webinar series on AMR challenges and One Health solutions across three regions, with a country spotlight on Nigeria. Discussions highlight critical gaps in political commitment, sustainable financing, and locally relevant evidence, particularly on antibiotic stewardship. Regional and country experiences demonstrate the importance of context-specific research, locally driven innovation, and stronger governance. Integrating these voices into global AMR governance is essential for a more equitable, effective, and enduring response.

items.title: Count the climate losses we prevent.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Université du Québec à Montréal, Montréal, QC, Canada. charpentier.arthur@uqam.ca.; Mathematics Department, Kyoto University, Kyoto, Japan. charpentier.arthur@uqam.ca.; Chaire PARI, Institut Louis Bachelier, Paris, France. charpentier.arthur@uqam.ca.

items.title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cardiovascular Medicine, Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. zengzhi86@smu.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. zengzhi86@smu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

items.title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Physics, Hefei University of Technology, Hefei, Anhui, China. hjli@hfut.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. Increasing the lattice period suppresses evanescent coupling between neighboring guided resonances, driving the system into the weak-coupling regime of a tight-binding model and producing flat dispersions along orthogonal in-plane directions. Breaking the in-plane mirror symmetry further imparts chirality without compromising the flat-band character. The resulting resonance remains robust over incidence angles of ±5° and across azimuthal directions, while maintaining a nearly invariant resonance wavelength, a Q-factor of 886 and a circular dichroism of 0.86. The chiral flatband further enhances third-harmonic generation, which inherits its spin selectivity and angular robustness, enabling chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a planar platform for omnidirectional chiral flat-band physics, nonlinear nanophotonics and imaging.

items.title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML), Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands.; Oxford Martin School, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK.
items.abstract: Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024-2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe's annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

items.title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere.
items.last_author_affiliation: Joint Genome Institute, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, USA. nckyrpides@lbl.gov.
items.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

items.title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Orogenic Belts and Crustal Evolution, School of Earth and Space Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, China. msli@pku.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Shale Oil and Gas Enrichment Mechanisms and Effective Development, Beijing, China. msli@pku.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth's largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

items.title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy.
items.last_author_affiliation: National Engineering Research Center for Nanomedicine, College of Life Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. zhiqiangluo@hust.edu.cn.; Department of Pediatric Surgery, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. zhiqiangluo@hust.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

items.title: Predicting follow-up cognition using estimated structural and functional connectivity networks and artificial intelligence in multiple sclerosis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Radiology, Weill Cornell Medicine, New York, NY, USA.; Computational Biology, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Brain's structural and functional connectomes (SC and FC) offer insights into the relationship between brain circuits and cognitive functioning in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). However, diffusion and functional MRI, which are used to extract SC and FC, is expensive and time consuming, therefore are not currently used in the clinical setting. Our prior work demonstrated that estimated SC and FC (eSC and eFC) generated using MS lesion masks and artificial intelligence (AI) models can predict disability as effectively as SC and FC derived from diffusion and functional MRI in MS. In this study, we identify the eSC and eFC brain circuits that are associated with baseline and 4-year follow-up cognition and assess the ability of eSC and eFC in predicting cognition in MS. In a cohort of 171 with MS, the Network Modification tool was performed to estimate SC from the MS lesion mask, which is extracted from structural MRI scans. The eSC was then used as an input to Krakencoder, an encoder-decoder model, to estimate FC. The highest accuracy was obtained when predicting follow-up Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) using regional eSC or eFC, with a median Spearman's correlation coefficient of 0.58 for eSC and 0.56 for eFC. Decreased eSC and eFC in the cerebellum and increased eFC in the default mode network were associated with lower follow-up SDMT scores. Our findings demonstrate that eSC and eFC derived from clinically acquired MRI and AI models can effectively predict cognition. The use of lesion-based estimates of connectomes may potentially inform clinical trials by identifying the specific brain circuits that could be targeted for the non-invasive treatments aimed at improving cognitive function in MS.

items.title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Translational Medicine, Precision Medicine Institute, The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China. chendm29@mail.sysu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3+ macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7-MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3-CDK7-MAFB-TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion.

items.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Chemo and Biosensing, College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, China. gbwen@hnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells.

items.title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medical Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden. kimmo.kartasalo@ki.se.; ELLIS Institute Finland, Espoo, Finland. kimmo.kartasalo@ki.se.; Department of Computing, Faculty of Technology, University of Turku, Turku, Finland. kimmo.kartasalo@ki.se.; Science for Life Laboratory (SciLifeLab), Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden. kimmo.kartasalo@ki.se.
items.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with-and is in some cases surpassed by-TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists' grading reaches quadratic Cohen's kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

items.title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels.
items.last_author_affiliation: Departamento de Entomologia, Instituto Aggeu Magalhães (IAM), Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz), Recife, Pernambuco, Brazil. gabriel.wallau@fiocruz.br.; Núcleo de Bioinformática, Instituto Aggeu Magalhães (IAM), Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz/PE), Recife, Brazil. gabriel.wallau@fiocruz.br.; Department of Arbovirology and Entomology, Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine, Hamburg, Germany. gabriel.wallau@fiocruz.br.; Universidade Federal de Santa Maria (UFSM), Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. gabriel.wallau@fiocruz.br.
items.abstract: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

items.title: Pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Orthopedics, The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Suzhou, China. szgengdc@suda.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

items.title: The plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 forms oligomeric complexes and senses broader proteolytic activity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Universitetsbyen 81, DK8000, Aarhus C, Denmark. gra@mbg.au.dk.
items.abstract: In self-perpetuating proteolytic cascades within the body, tight regulation by an excess of inhibitors is essential to maintain homoeostasis. The plasma protein inter-α-trypsin inhibitor heavy chain 4 (ITIH4) inhibits extracellular proteolytic pathways, including the contact system and the complement cascade, by a mechanism requiring cleavage of ITIH4 but without direct binding to the active site of the cleaving protease. The structural and mechanistic details of the cleavage-induced changes in ITIH4 that lead to protease inhibition remain elusive. Here, we show that ITIH4 undergoes an unexpectedly large, conformational change upon cleavage involving complete unfolding of an immunoglobulin domain and a reorganisation of the N-terminal F3 domain. The cleaved N-terminal fragment of ITIH4 (ITIH4N) forms ultra stable homo-oligomers with as many as seven ITIH4N molecules attached to the inhibited protease. This homo-interaction mimics the initial binding event with the cleaving protease. Mutation-induced disruption of homo-oligomerization leads to direct attachment of multiple ITIH4N molecules to different residues on the same protease and does not compromise inhibition, pointing to a function of ITIH4N oligomerization beyond protease inhibition. While proteolysis of ITIH4 may lead to inhibition of the cleaving protease, we show that nascent ITIH4N may associate with a molecule different from the cleaving protease or an existing protease-ITIH4N complex. Our data provide a comprehensive structural foundation for establishing a mechanistic framework for the function of ITIH4 and drive the future analysis of its in vivo function.

items.title: Scoop-shaped pores change how pollen is released from poricidal flowers.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Botany and Biodiversity Research, University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria.
items.abstract: Approximately 10% of angiosperms have poricidal flowers where pollen can only be released via a narrow aperture upon mechanical perturbations. Although the morphology of pore-like apertures likely determines how pollen is released and placed on pollinators, the functional significance of pore diversity remains unknown. Here, we establish critical baseline knowledge on pore morphological diversity across 523 species from six poricidal families, finding that pores either carry scoop-shaped modifications or do not. Using artificial pollen release experiments, we demonstrate functional differences, with scoop-bearing species having narrower, faster-moving pollen streams than non-scoop-bearing species. In a selected scoop-bearing species, we further demonstrate that the functionality of scoop-shaped pores is sensitive to variation in mechanical perturbations, with low-frequency vibrations expelling larger quantities of pollen with a more dispersed pollen cloud than high-frequency vibrations. In conclusion, differences in pore morphology may critically determine the accuracy of pollen placement on pollinators, making pore morphology a hitherto overlooked trait in flowers relying on aerosolization of pollen grains.

items.title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medicine, Columbia University Irving Medical Center, New York, NY, USA. iat1@columbia.edu.; Department of Physiology and Cellular Biophysics, Columbia University Irving Medical Center, New York, NY, USA. iat1@columbia.edu.; Department of Pathology, Columbia University Irving Medical Center, New York, NY, USA. iat1@columbia.edu.
items.abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

items.title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits.
items.last_author_affiliation: James C. Wyant College of Optical Sciences, University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona, USA. Matt.Eichenfield@colorado.edu.; Microsystems Engineering, Science, and Applications, Sandia National Laboratories, Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA. Matt.Eichenfield@colorado.edu.; Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering, University of Colorado, Boulder, Colorado, USA. Matt.Eichenfield@colorado.edu.
items.abstract: Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

items.title: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electronic and Computer Engineering, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong, China. eeyajing@ust.hk.; HKUST Shenzhen Research Institute, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. eeyajing@ust.hk.
items.abstract: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Current smart toothbrush systems fundamentally fail to capture the critical fine-scale biomechanics at the bristle-tooth interface, which is essential for evaluating clinical adherence and preventing gingival damage. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing monitoring and quantitative feedback. These results establish embedded co-deformation sensing and AI-based interpretation as a technical foundation for future personalized toothbrushing assessment and coaching.

items.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Centre for Materials Science and Nanotechnology, University of Oslo, PO Box 1033 Blindern, NO-0315, Oslo, Norway. jonathan.polfus@kjemi.uio.no.
items.abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3-δ, as shown by  atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

items.title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves.
items.last_author_affiliation: Hubrecht Institute-KNAW (Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences), University Medical Center Utrecht, Utrecht, The Netherlands. k.sonnen@hubrecht.eu.
items.abstract: Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

items.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Mathematics and Physics, North China Electric Power University, Beijing, 102206, China. tianyh@lzu.edu.cn.; School of Physical Science and Technology, Lanzhou University, Lanzhou, Gansu, 730000, China. tianyh@lzu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ/10 and annular features smaller than λ/60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

items.title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Psychology, University of Fribourg, Fribourg, Switzerland. salome.kurth@unifr.ch.; Department of Pulmonology, University Hospital Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland. salome.kurth@unifr.ch.
items.abstract: The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio - a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment - as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

items.title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription.
items.last_author_affiliation: Program in Cellular & Molecular Medicine, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.; Department of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.; Department of Biophysics, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.; Jenkins Biophysics Program, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.; Program in Cell, Molecular, Developmental Biology, and Biophysics, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.; Department of Biology, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. sua.myong@childrens.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Biomolecular condensates have been proposed to enhance transcription by locally concentrating polymerases and cofactors, often through intrinsically disordered proteins. However, the functional role of phase separation and the molecular connections between RNA and the transcription machinery remain poorly defined. Using T7 RNA polymerase (T7 RNAP), which lacks intrinsic disorder, together with FUS, which does not directly interact with T7 RNAP, we dissect the mechanisms by which FUS enhances transcription. We find that monomeric FUS is sufficient to stimulate transcription, whereas condensate formation contributes only a modest additional effect. FUS is recruited selectively to active transcription complexes through binding to nascent RNA, assembling into a dynamic nanoscale structure that enhances RNAP loading and stabilizes the transcription initiation bubble. Furthermore, FUS suppresses inhibitory R-loop formation, thereby accelerating elongation. Together, these findings identify nascent RNA as the central organizing element through which FUS modulates transcription via specific molecular interactions, largely independent of phase separation.

items.title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine, Heilongjiang Bayi Agricultural University, Daqing, PR China. dongbosun@126.com.
items.abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

items.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Infectious Diseases, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA. Hyeryun.Choe@childrens.harvard.edu.; Department of Pediatrics, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. Hyeryun.Choe@childrens.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

items.title: scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery.
items.last_author_affiliation: Faculty of Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology, Shenzhen, China. qz.lian@siat.ac.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Quantitative Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen Institute of Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, China. qz.lian@siat.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. We introduce scBOA, a two-stage framework that uses Bayesian optimization to select workflow parameters against a prespecified objective and reruns the selected configuration for reference-assisted analysis. Its configurable objectives combine annotation purity, marker concordance and transcriptomic cohesion, enabling fine-grained or conservative solutions. Optional extensions support low-confidence-cell refinement and multi-sample integration. Across simulations and fluorescence-activated cell sorting datasets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreas and adult heart, we compare Gaussian-process scBOA with 14 alternative parameter-selection and clustering strategies. We show that performance depends on the objective, workflow, reference hierarchy and vocabulary, consensus-label construction and partition granularity. We find that scBOA is not uniformly superior, but shows strong aggregate performance when annotation targets align with biological structure. We apply a mouse Huntington's disease dataset as an exploratory stress test of integration and reference mapping. Overall, we demonstrate that scBOA provides reproducible, objective-driven workflow optimization for reference-assisted single-cell analysis.

items.title: Plants recognize identity and intensity of herbivores to adaptively reconfigure metabolism.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. yousjoo@snu.ac.kr.; Institute for Data Innovation in Science, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. yousjoo@snu.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Plant specialized metabolites play central roles in defending against herbivorous insects. Yet, how the diversity of phytochemicals contributes to defense across different contexts of herbivory remains incompletely understood. Here, we analyse the leaf metabolome of Arabidopsis thaliana exposed to four herbivore species at three attack intensities to determine the herbivore-specific metabolic responses. We show species-specific and intensity-dependent metabolic patterns that exceed differences expected from feeding guild or host range, both among different metabolic pathways and within the glucosinolate biosynthetic pathway. Mutant analyses further reveal that metabolic specificity arises from distinct contributions of phytohormonal signaling and membrane-associated receptor complexes. Through 520 matched metabolome-bioassay pairs, we identify putative herbivore-resistant metabolites that are preferentially induced by the corresponding herbivore species; these responses are diminished in membrane coreceptor mutants. Together, our results highlight multiple dimensions of metabolic diversity and specificity in plant defenses and demonstrate their functional consequences with unprecedented coverage and resolution.

items.title: An intragastric murine model that recapitulates natural infection with invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella for preclinical evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity and protection.
items.abstract: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease is a major global health concern, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where young children and immunocompromised individuals are particularly vulnerable. Preclinical models that reproduce the natural course of invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella infection without antibiotic-mediated disruption of the intestinal microbiota are essential for vaccine development. Here, an antibiotic-free murine model is described based on intragastric infection of susceptible C57BL/6 mice with the ST313 clinical isolate Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium D23580. Over seven days, infection progressed from intestinal colonization to extraintestinal dissemination, accompanied by increasing histopathological damage and activation of local and systemic inflammatory responses. The ability of the infection model to evaluate vaccine-induced immunity and protection was assessed by immunizing mice with a formalin-inactivated D23580 strain. Vaccination elicited Salmonella-specific serum IgG and reduced clinical severity, with vaccinated mice showing significantly lower bacterial loads in blood, liver and colon compared with control mice after intragastric challenge. By combining the enteric route, which mimics the natural route of human infection, with an intact intestinal microbiota, this model reproduces key features of progressive invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease and provides a tool for investigating host-pathogen interactions and evaluating vaccine-induced immunity and protection.

items.title: HER3 mediates metabolic reprogramming in metastatic colorectal and pancreatic cancer
items.abstract: Liver metastases are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet the oncogenic signals that shape tumor metabolism in the hepatic niche remain poorly understood. Here, we show that HER3 activation drives a liver metastasis-specific glycolytic program in both cancer types. Genetic or pharmacological HER3 inhibition suppresses cancer glycolysis while increasing dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), rendering liver metastases vulnerable to OXPHOS inhibition. Combining the HER3 inhibitor sapitinib with distinct OXPHOS inhibitors led to in vitro synergy and durable tumor-free survival in orthotopic CRC and PDAC liver metastases models, with further validation in patient-derived xenografts. Mechanistically, HER3 promotes glycolysis through activating PFK2 and reduces OXPHOS through activating DRP1-mediated mitochondrial remodeling, both pathways were activated in liver metastases compared to matched primary tumors. Together, our findings identify the HER3-AKT/RSK-PFK2 axis as a driver of glycolysis and metastatic growth and reveal an OXPHOS dependency induced by HER3 inhibition that may be exploited through combined HER3 and OXPHOS targeting in metastatic CRC and PDAC.

items.title: Multi-layer colocalization prioritizes adipose RNA regulatory features beyond gene expression at type 2 diabetes loci
items.corresponding_institution: College of Electronics & Information Engineering,Jinggangshan University
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) genetic signals reside predominantly in non-coding regions, and linking them to molecular mechanisms requires resolving the RNA phenotypes through which they act in disease-relevant tissues. Adipose tissue is central to systemic glucose homeostasis, yet most colocalization studies have relied on total gene expression, which captures only one dimension of RNA regulation. Here, we integrated 338 fine-mapped T2D signals from DIAMANTE with five GTEx RNA measurements-gene expression, exon expression, transcript usage, transcriptional-event usage, and splice-junction usage-across subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue from the eQTL Catalogue. Enforcing bilateral posterior coverage and a cumulative posterior selection rule across 13,216 admissible comparisons expanded testable T2D signals from 253 with gene expression alone to 293 and identified 77 colocalized pairs defining 38 signal-gene relationships across 30 T2D signals, with 87.0% of retained pairs involving non-gene-expression features. At loci with direct same-gene comparators, including BDNF-AS and PGM1, specific RNA features strongly colocalized with T2D while bulk gene expression favored distinct causal variants, demonstrating that gene-level analysis alone can miss or misattribute the primary regulatory signal. Locus-resolved fine-mapping linked a BDNF-AS splice junction to rs6265 in both depots and narrowed PGM1 and RCCD1 to shared or nested candidate-variant sets around defined transcript anchors. External adipose cohorts provided complementary support, single-nucleus and cell-class eQTL data defined cellular contexts, and metabolic-trait and multi-tissue analyses distinguished insulin-resistance (IRS1), fat-distribution (CCDC92), and cross-tissue adiposity (BDNF-AS) profiles. Together, these results provide a multi-layer adipose regulatory atlas that converts T2D signals into specific RNA features, candidate variants, cellular settings, and measurement-led routes for functional validation.

items.title: Rapid, behaviorally timed increases in blood-brain barrier permeability are predicted by endothelial calcium events and driven by histaminergic axons
items.abstract: Survival requires a detailed understanding of body state, and the vasculature provides a continuous conduit of this information to the brain. Yet the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is canonically viewed as a stable boundary, and any passage across it as pathological leak, because sustained exposure carries real risk. How the forebrain resolves these competing needs for information versus safety remains unknown. Here we show that the healthy barrier opens briefly and locally at moments when body-state information may be worth the risk. Using two-photon imaging of an intravascular dextran in the somatosensory neocortex of mice performing a cued reward task, we identified Plume Events: transient, focal increases in permeability at penetrating arterioles that were locked to the cue and reward, persisted on trials without detectable dilation, and shifted earlier with training. Endothelial calcium events preceded and predicted Plume Events within seconds and within 15 micrometers of the vessel wall. Histaminergic axons from the tuberomammillary nucleus were active before Plume Events, and their optogenetic stimulation drove Plume Events that waned across repeated trains while dilation persisted. Together, these findings reframe the blood-brain barrier as a dynamic interface whose openings are immediate, local and transactional, granting the forebrain access to body-state signals at behaviorally relevant moments. Such events may also support brain health through locally timed metabolic supply and waste clearance.

items.title: PD-1 inhibition drives CD8 T cell recruitment and T cell-dependent myeloid remodeling in responsive tumors
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
items.abstract: While leukocyte recruitment is central to anti-tumor immunity, how recruitment changes over time and following perturbation with immunotherapy is poorly understood because of a lack of tools to identify recruited leukocytes. We used intravenous antibody labeling to characterize recruited leukocytes in murine tumors and evaluated how programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) impacted recruitment. Early PD-1 ICI administration, which induced robust tumor control, increased the density of recently recruited CD8 T cells, and these T cells exhibited a less-exhausted phenotype compared to unlabeled intratumoral CD8 T cells. Early PD-1 ICI also caused a shift in myeloid populations to a proinflammatory iNOS positive phenotype. Delaying PD-1 ICI resulted in ineffective tumor control, which was associated with reduced leukocyte entry per unit volume, less granzyme B upregulation in CD8 T cells, and less iNOS induction in myeloid cells. Use of FTY720 to prevent lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes abolished the protective effects of early PD-1 ICI and reduced CD8 T cell recruitment. While FTY720 did not impact myeloid cell recruitment, it did reduce myeloid iNOS induction. Lastly, PD-1 deletion in CD8 T cells was sufficient to increase CD8 T cell recruitment to tumors and iNOS expression in myeloid cells. These data suggest that CD8 T cell recruitment both increases the quantity and quality of CD8 T cells in the tumor and drives T cell-driven remodeling of the myeloid compartment. These findings support efforts to develop therapies that promote CD8 T cell recruitment to improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: OTU Taxa: a taxonomy aware pretrained model for 16S microbiome profiles
items.corresponding_institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
items.abstract: Background: Microbiome profiles combine sequence-derived units with taxonomy. Pretrained models use different community vocabularies and are often evaluated on few labels, leaving their value under broad competitive evaluation unclear. We introduce OTU-Taxa, which pairs operational taxonomic unit (OTU) identity with hierarchical taxonomy during autoregressive pretraining on unlabeled profiles. Results: In an in-domain evaluation across 250 Microbe Atlas Project (MAP)-derived classification tasks with disjoint folds, mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.744 for OTU-Taxa and 0.749 for Random Forest. OTU-Taxa was the highest-ranked pretrained method; Nemenyi comparisons did not detect rank differences from Random Forest across the three metrics. The model also generated largely non-copied profiles and recovered more withheld community members at larger cutoffs, while retrieval gave stronger empirical fidelity and early ranking. It also supported abundance-rank readouts and recovered higher-rank classifier assignments from sample context for known-vocabulary OTUs under controlled sequence degradation, although agreement was limited at genus and species ranks. Conclusions: Within the MAP 97% closed-reference 16S vocabulary, the pretrained representation supports in-domain prediction of metadata labels alongside generative and taxonomic readouts. Supervised abundance models, empirical retrieval, and intact-sequence classifiers remain stronger choices for several corresponding endpoints, while OTU-Taxa provides one shared contextual representation across all four analyses.

items.title: Determinants of domain-specific cognitive impairment after stroke: a mega-analysis of 13 acute ischaemic stroke cohorts
authors: Schaper, F. L. W. V. J.
items.abstract: The relationship between brain lesions and cognition is enigmatic. Apparently similar lesions can produce different outcomes. Stroke provides a prototypical model to understand how lesion anatomy, network disruption, prior injury and patient characteristics shape impairment. We analysed 3,034 patients from 13 acute ischaemic stroke cohorts, integrating infarct size and location, structural and functional lesion network mapping, pre-existing cerebrovascular injury, and demographic and clinical characteristics to predict impairment across six cognitive domains within one year after stroke. Infarct topography and connectivity improved prediction for six of seven outcomes over demographic, clinical and infarct-size information alone. Structural lesion connectivity accounted for most gains, with additional gains from topography and connectivity of pre-existing vascular lesions. Across domains, gains rested on left anterior thalamic connectivity plus domain-specific anatomy. Our findings establish, at unprecedented scale, that understanding lesion-cognition relationships requires looking beyond the lesion to networks, prior brain pathology and individual context.

items.title: EditFinder: A Sequence-Based Model for A-to-I RNA Editing Identification and Characterization of Genetic Variant Effects
items.abstract: A-to-I RNA editing is a widespread post-transcriptional modification that contributes to transcriptomic diversity and has been implicated in various diseases. However, incomplete reference resources for RNA editing and limited research into its genetic regulation hinder investigations into RNA editing-mediated disease mechanisms. To address these limitations, EditFinder, a sequence-based model for identifying A-to-I RNA editing sites and assessing the effects of genetic variants on RNA editing, is developed. EditFinder demonstrates superior performance on both an independent reference validation dataset and a read-based sequencing dataset. Its genome-wide application generates an expanded resource of candidate A-to-I RNA editing sites, providing a foundation for comprehensive exploration and functional annotation of RNA editing. Beyond site identification, EditFinder enables systematic assessment of the position- and nucleotide-dependent effects of genetic variations on predicted editing probabilities, highlighting the particularly strong influence of the 3'-adjacent nucleotide. Analysis of REDIportal-documented editing sites further suggests that genetic variations in flanking sequences may alter the predicted editing status of approximately 10% of the entries. Moreover, changes in EditFinder-predicted editing probabilities may reflect trends in SNP-associated variation in RNA editing frequency. Collectively, EditFinder provides a valuable resource for investigating RNA editing and its genetic regulation related to human diseases.

items.title: Even more space efficient genome sketching with Lash
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatrics, School of Medicine, University of California San Diego
items.abstract: Advances in sequencing technology have driven an exponential growth in microbial genomic data, making exact pairwise distance computation increasingly impractical at scale. As a result, computationally efficient genomic distance estimation algorithms have become an essential alternative, e.g., sketching algorithms such as HyperLogLog and MinHash. Here, we present Lash, a software that provides UltraLogLog and ExaLogLog (more space-efficient variants of the HyperLogLog structure) and HyperMinHash (a more space-efficient variant of a MinHash structure) as methods to approximate genomic distance. UltraLogLog and ExaLogLog were demonstrated to be around 28% and 43% more space/memory-efficient respectively than HyperLogLog, and HyperMinHash was 4-5 times more space/memory-efficient than MinHash for various genome comparison tasks.

items.title: Unscored variants leave many comparisons of variant effect predictors undecided: evidence from ClinVar, published benchmarks and genomic language models
items.corresponding_institution: Faculty of Biological and Veterinary Sciences, Institute of Veterinary Medicine, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Torun, 87-100 Torun, Poland
items.abstract: Background. Variant effect predictors leave different variants unscored, so reported accuracies often rest on different variants, and which predictor is better can depend on variants never scored. Results. Manski's sharp bounds contain each predictor's accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) whatever its unscored variants would score. A comparison is decided when the two bounds are disjoint, which cannot happen when the two shares scored (of variants or, for AUROC, pathogenic-benign pairs) sum to one or less. For 49 dbNSFP predictors on 328,328 ClinVar substitutions, 745 of 1,176 comparisons are undecided inside declared scopes and 1,093 on the whole panel. In ten benchmarks from one PubMed query, 1,045 of 2,842 stated orderings (36.8%) are undecided. Yet most orderings between well-known predictors are decided (177 of 287), among them AlphaMissense above REVEL in the sixth Critical Assessment of Genome Interpretation. AlphaMissense's canonical-transcript release scores no missense substitution in secondary-findings genes CALM1, CALM2 or WT1, and missense variants that REVEL's and AlphaMissense's releases leave unscored are pathogenic less often than the panel's (likelihood ratios 0.18 and 0.25, describing each release). Across nine species, the genomic language model Evo 2 does not outperform gene annotation (species-mean AUROC 0.943 against 0.958); its 8,192-bp margin is resolved over Ensembl's conservation track (+0.108) but not over the 241-mammal phyloP (+0.055). Conclusions. Benchmarks should report each predictor's reach (share of variants scored) per label class and which orderings the bounds decide; the deposited reach matrices and glmtrust package allow these checks without rescoring.

items.title: Pharmacodynamic encoding of tumor exposure identifies a mesenchymal state associated with antitumor sensitivity
items.corresponding_institution: Research and Development, Oncology Business Unit, PharmaMar, 28770, Madrid, Spain
items.abstract: Predictive biomarker discovery in oncology relies on response phenotypes that do not account for tumor-site drug exposure. Here we developed PHENIX, a model informed framework that uses tumor exposure driven pharmacodynamic parameters as quantitative phenotypes for molecular-state discovery. Using PM534, a colchicine site tubulin inhibitor, we integrated measured drug concentrations with physiologically based pharmacokinetic and longitudinal pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic modeling. This yielded K2, quantifying the efficiency with which intratumoral exposure is converted into tumor damage across cell-derived xenograft models. Higher K2 was associated with a mesenchymal state enriched for epithelial to mesenchymal transition, focal adhesion and extracellular matrix programs. An interpretable pathway based model retained epithelial to mesenchymal transition and focal adhesion as candidate features and showed preliminary cross dataset transferability. Proteomic analyses supported this molecular axis, whereas projection across CCLE and TCGA mapped its occurrence in cancer contexts. Patient derived orthotopic xenograft profiling provided orthogonal in vivo support. PHENIX demonstrates the feasibility of using model derived pharmacodynamic parameters as molecular phenotypes for tumor state discovery.

items.title: Evolutionary rescue of rare human genetic disorders in yeast models
items.abstract: Several thousand human disease-associated genes have clear yeast orthologs, making yeast an ideal model system for advancing a basic understanding of human disease. We used CRISPR-Cas9 editing to generate 51 yeast strains with 11 human disease-associated variants, focusing on human disease genes involved in protein glycosylation, ribosome maturation, mitochondrial function, and RNA regulation. We find that most of these alleles recapitulate as fitness defects in yeast. To enrich for suppressors, we evolved these populations for 1,000 generations and performed whole genome sequencing. We identified both known and previously unknown suppressor mutations. For example, we identify mutations in DPM1 and RPS9B that compensate for disease phenotypes of ALG7 and SDO1, respectively. Reconstructed strains harboring evolved suppressor mutations and the original disease alleles demonstrate that these suppressors rescue fitness and may compensate for defects in molecular function. By exerting continuous selective pressure over thousands of generations, experimental evolution allows us to select for suppressor mutations, including those with modest fitness effects or occurring at lower frequencies, which are underrepresented in traditional genetic screens. Our results map local genetic interaction networks centered around disease-associated alleles, providing greater insights into disease phenotypes and informing potential targeted therapies for disease management in patients with rare disorders.

items.title: SingloCell: an open and accessible web platform for multimodal single-cell data exploration
items.abstract: Single-cell research is transforming biology and medicine, offering unprecedented insight into health and disease. Yet, the true potential of single-cell data can only be realized when datasets are open, easy to interact with, and accessible to all. We introduce SingloCell (https://singlocell.openscience.mcgill.ca/), an intuitive multimodal single-cell web platform built on three principles: accessibility, interactivity and traceability. SingloCell provides free browser-based access to single-cell datasets and supports user submission of suspension-based transcriptomics, proteomics, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-derived gene activity matrices), immune receptor (BCR, TCR) and multi-omics modalities, as well as spatial datasets. This enables researchers, clinicians, educators, and the broader community to explore high-dimensional datasets without programming expertise. Users can explore and analyse data in real time using tools for differential gene expression, functional enrichment, and pathway visualisation, while also examining pre-computed analyses such as pseudotime trajectories and cell-cell interactions. Datasets can be shared publicly or via unlisted links, and analytical workflows are documented through downloadable receipts.

items.title: Senescence-associated stromal remodeling in bone marrow aging and hematologic and bone-metastatic diseases
items.abstract: Cellular senescence is implicated as a driver of age-related tissue dysfunction and chronic inflammation. However, no single marker defines a senescent cell, and distinguishing senescence from other stressors requires both experimental perturbation and comparison across contexts. As part of the Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet), we generated a multimodal atlas integrating human bone marrow from 80 donors (54 assayed by single-cell RNA sequencing; 48 by Xenium spatial transcriptomics) with a 130 combined cases across four disease cohorts: breast and prostate cancer bone metastases (BCa/PCa; n=61), myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN; n=21), and multiple myeloma (MM; n=48). Human marrow aging was characterized by interferon and IL6/JAK/STAT3 activation in hematopoietic progenitors, myeloid-biased output, and progressive loss of naive CD4 T cell identity. Spatially, CDKN1A was concentrated in vascular stroma, and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) expression rose with age coordinately across stromal cell types within individual donors (mean pairwise rho = 0.46), consistent with shared influences on stromal aging. Malignancy was associated with distinct and disease-specific senescence-associated states rather than uniform amplification of aging programs. Senescent fibroblasts spatially adjacent to tumor in breast and prostate cancer bone metastases shared an upregulated secretory program comprising 148 genes encoding secreted proteins, alongside upregulated matrix-remodeling and cellular adhesion signatures. Osteolineage cells found in metastasis sites as well as in MPN marrow also displayed distinct senescence-associated phenotypes, including enlarged, multinucleated osteoclasts and CDKN1A+ osteoblasts with upregulated secretory programs. However, senescence-associated secretory programs and matrix dysregulation in stromal cells was not observed in MM, indicating that these features are not generic consequences of tumor burden within the bone marrow but rather arise from specific cancer-stromal interactions. Residual hematopoietic regions showed altered myeloid and erythroid composition and transcriptional states. To complement these human datasets, we used a mouse model in which doxorubicin-induced senescence reproduced molecular and compositional hallmarks of marrow aging that were selectively reversible with senolytic treatment. These data establish normal marrow as a quantitative baseline for senescence and separate shared from context-specific senescent states.

items.title: Monitoring cancer evolution under iatrogenic selection pressure by cellular liquid biopsy.
items.corresponding_institution: Experimental Medicine and Therapy Research, University of Regensburg, Regensburg, Germany
items.abstract: Cell-free liquid biopsy (LB) provides information about real-time tumor burden in cancer patients. In contrast, cellular LB can resolve the co-occurrence of actionable mutations within individual CTCs and their clonal architecture, revealing emerging treatment opportunities, information increasingly needed as the number of available drugs grows. Here, we describe a case with repeated blood sampling and CTC analysis using a single-cell-adapted IMPACT assay (scIMPACT). We observed therapeutically relevant alterations and clonal shifts arising in response to selected therapies. Applied systematically, such analyses have the power to uncover cellular adaptations to therapy-induced selection pressures and enable flexible treatment adjustments to evolving disease.

items.title: Effects of Zika Virus Non-Structural Proteins on the Innate Antiviral Response.
items.corresponding_institution: Arizona State University, School of Biological and Health Systems Engineering
items.abstract: Innate immune pathways are therapeutic targets of prime importance, both for antiviral and neurodegenerative therapies. The Zika virus is highly evolved to manipulate these same pathways so expertly that half of infections go unnoticed. While the direct inhibition of immune effectors by ZIKV nonstructural proteins is well characterized, second order effects on immune responsive cellular functions are less understood. We induced the innate antiviral response in human microglia like cells, perturbed that response using 6 ZIKV nonstructural genes, and resolve systems level effects using scRNA-seq and hdWGCNA. We recapitulate known ZIKV bioactivity and identify specific suppression of the PA28 immunoproteasome by NS2B, demonstrating how ZIKV can shape tissue level neuroinflammation.
