Unexpectedly, we found the splicing-associated domain, H3K36me3, and splicing factors including U2af38 and Cdc5, are also enriched near the NLB, suggesting that splicing may be spatially undertaken within this compartment. Together, our findings reveal a spatial organization of nascent RNA in which DNA-associated exon sequences and compacted intronic transcripts are coordinated with distinct transcriptional and RNA-processing subnuclear domains. We propose that such spatial segregation may be commonly utilized in broad cellular genes.

items.title: An Unconventional Targeting Architecture Directs Cardiolipin Synthase to Multiple Compartments
items.corresponding_institution: National Institute of Science Education and Research-HBNI
items.abstract: Multi-compartment protein targeting underlies the functional and metabolic flexibility of eukaryotic cells. However, how a single targeting region directs a protein to multiple cellular compartments remains poorly understood. A good example is membrane lipid biosynthesis: cardiolipin is normally synthesized in the mitochondrial inner membrane but has also been detected in the nuclear envelope of Tetrahymena. Here, we show that Tetrahymena cardiolipin synthase (TtCLS) localises to three distinct compartments. Systematic evolutionary and cell-biological analyses uncover a lineage-specific C-terminal targeting signal that expands the subcellular distribution of TtCLS across mitochondria, nuclear envelope and plasma membrane. We further show that its dynamic distribution among these compartments is regulated by phosphorylation. This multifunctional targeting architecture contains an amphipathic helix implicated in membrane association, which is structurally conserved across bacterial and eukaryotic CLS_PLD enzymes. Notably, this architecture remains compatible with conserved mitochondrial import systems across evolutionarily distant eukaryotes. Together, these findings uncover a previously unknown targeting architecture in which a single C-terminal region integrates overlapping and potentially regulatable localization determinants to target one protein across three different membrane systems.

items.title: Rab29 GTPase is a specific cargo transport receptor to enhance COPII recruitment and anterograde trafficking of nascent GPCRs at ER
items.abstract: Rab GTPases are the master players in the cellular transport system, but their function and regulation in cargo recruitment to COPII vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are unknown. Here, we demonstrate that Rab29 inhibition via genetic deletion and inactivation markedly impedes the ER-to-Golgi transport, cell surface expression, and cellular functions of a subset of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). More interestingly, Rab29 inhibition substantially attenuates GPCR concentration and recruitment kinetics at ER-derived COPII vesicles without affecting vesicle biogenesis. We also show that activated Rab29 localizes to the ER and COPII vesicles where it directly interacts with both its cargo GPCRs and all four Sec24 isoforms. We further identify a specific motif that mediates the interaction of angiotensin II type 2 receptor (AT2R) with Rab29; mutating this motif effectively blocks AT2R recruitment into COPII vesicles and compromises its delivery to the cell surface. Collectively, these data indicate that Rab29 is the first Rab functioning as a specific cargo transport receptor to enhance COPII capture and anterograde trafficking of GPCRs from the ER which is mediated through activation-dependent interactions with both Sec24 and cargo GPCRs and identify a novel function for the Rab family in membrane trafficking.

items.title: F1FO-ATP synthase subunit DAPIT rewires mitochondrial metabolism in cancer cells to drive cellular hyperproliferation
items.abstract: Mitochondrial ATP synthase is the main source of cellular ATP. Its assembly into dimers and oligomers is modulated by several subunits. While subunits e and g promote dimerization, DAPIT (USMG5) stabilizes dimer-dimer interactions. Whether DAPIT (diabetes associated protein in insulin-sensitive tissues) also controls ATP synthase function remained unknown. Using high-resolution live-cell imaging, metabolic profiling, mass spectrometry, and molecular genetics methods, we show that DAPIT-dependent dimer stabilization delays enzyme turnover and optimizes ATP synthesis. This structural role extends beyond bioenergetics: by coupling mitochondrial energy conversion to metabolic restructuring, DAPIT enables the upregulation of glycolysis and efficient shunting of substrates toward oxidative phosphorylation. This allows cells to sustain energy metabolism without activating stress responses. Our findings establish DAPIT as a molecular link between ATP synthase architecture and metabolic adaptation, with implications for understanding mitochondrial remodeling in proliferating and differentiating cells.

items.title: Multi-colour smFISH with automated cell-cycle quantification reveals distinct localization of co-regulated cell wall mRNAs in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast
items.corresponding_institution: Institite for Cell Biology and Centre for Engineering Biology, School of Biological Sciences, University of Edinburgh
items.abstract: Every aspect of messenger RNA life and fate is dictated by its complementary bound proteins. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate mRNA localization, translation, and/or degradation, and mRNAs encoding functionally related proteins can form "RNA regulons" that are bound by shared sets of RBPs. Here, we present an open-source multi-colour smFISH-based workflow we developed to systematically quantify mRNA abundance and localization across the budding yeast cell cycle. With this workflow, we investigate the cell-cycle dependent regulation of mRNAs encoding cell wall proteins (cwmRNAs) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast. We quantify the localization of SRL1 and SUN4 cwmRNAs which are bound by Ssd1, Mpt5/Puf5, and She2-She3 among other RBPs. We show that SRL1 and SUN4 exhibit distinct cell cycle-dependent abundance and localization patterns, and that SRL1 mRNA relies on She2 and She3 and partially Ssd1, but not Mpt5, for its localization to the bud. Our results argue that Ssd1 and Mpt5 are not primarily RNA localization factors and confirm the importance of the She2-She3 complex in conferring bud-localization to diverse mRNAs. We also show that SUN4 and SRL1 mRNA localization is not affected by the Sec complex which facilitates the localization of their protein products. These findings show that co-regulated mRNAs can follow distinct spatiotemporal programs, and our workflow provides a general framework to test how RNA-binding proteins coordinate mRNA localization in single cells.

items.title: A TRAIL-R4 splice isoform sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-induced apoptosis
items.abstract: The immune system can recognize and eliminate tumor cells through the secretion of specific cytokines, including TRAIL (tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand). TRAIL triggers apoptosis by binding to its death receptors, TRAIL-R1 and TRAIL-R2. However, cancer cells can evade TRAIL-mediated cell death through the expression of decoy receptors, TRAIL-R3 and TRAIL-R4, which can bind TRAIL but lack the ability to initiate apoptotic signaling. Here, we focused on the decoy receptor TRAIL-R4, also known as TNFRSF10D, and investigated an alternative splicing event that generates a transcript lacking exon 3. This exon-skipping event results in a truncated receptor isoform, termed iTRAIL-R4, which lacks part of the ligand-binding domain. Structural biology analyses confirmed that TRAIL cannot efficiently bind to iTRAIL-R4. Interestingly, whereas the canonical TRAIL-R4 isoform protects cancer cells against TRAIL-induced apoptosis, overexpression of iTRAIL-R4 sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-mediated cell death. Furthermore, combining iTRAIL-R4 expression with different therapeutic treatments enhances the sensitivity of cancer cells. Collectively, our findings highlight the potential of iTRAIL-R4 to help counteract therapeutic cancer resistance and recurrence. They further support the therapeutic relevance of modulating TRAIL-R4 alternative splicing to shift cancer cells toward a more apoptosis-sensitive state.

items.title: isoGS: A genomic method to navigate the breeder's dilemma of diversity versus eliteness
items.abstract: Global networks of public crop breeding programs exchange germplasm to share traits and increase diversity for genetic gain. There is a fundamental dilemma in crop breeding between the need to expand the genetic variation in elite gene pools while avoiding disruptions to essential traits required for eliteness. One particular challenge in admixed germplasm is the release of undesired transgressive segregation due to the disruption of favorable epistatic haplotypes of essential traits, which may stymie deployment of genomic selection (GS) In this study, we used breeding simulations to model recurrent population improvement for an annual crop species that can be selfed and crossed to examine the effectiveness of GS in admixed germplasm. We quantified the genetic heterogeneity between founder lines with an isoeliteness score, an effect size-weighted Hamming distance using quantitative trait loci markers. Populations with low founder isoeliteness (i.e. low genetic compatibility) had lower genetic gain with GS in early cycles than those with high founder isoeliteness (63% and 27% lower after 2 and 4 cycles). To mitigate this, we developed an isoeliteness-guided GS (isoGS) method to recover favorable epistatic haplotypes in a segregating population, which enabled 31% and 15% more genetic gain after 4 and 20 cycles. Our results suggest that founder isoeliteness scores and isoGS are valuable tools for overcoming the diversity vs. eliteness dilemma by managing the introduction of genetic diversity in a trait-specific manner.

items.title: A switch in Nrg1-Rtg3 promoter recruitment coordinates mitochondrial cristae remodeling during the diauxic transition
items.abstract: During the diauxic transition, Saccharomyces cerevisiae must preserve mitochondrial genome integrity while remodeling mitochondrial architecture for respiratory growth. The transcription factors Nrg1 and Rtg3 form a heteromeric regulator previously shown to be required for mitochondrial DNA maintenance, but its mitochondrial targets remained unknown. Here, we identify ILV5 and MGM101, which encode mitochondrial nucleoid proteins, as Nrg1-Rtg3 targets. Both factors occupied these promoters, with Rtg3 binding independently and recruiting Nrg1, providing a direct regulatory link to mitochondrial DNA maintenance. Unexpectedly, electron microscopy revealed that loss of either factor caused severe cristae defects even during fermentative growth, and these defects were more pronounced after the diauxic transition. Nrg1-Rtg3 also switched from repressing ATP20, ATP21, and MIC60 during fermentative growth to activating them after the transition. At the ATP20 promoter, recruitment dependence also reversed across the diauxic transition, from Nrg1-dependent recruitment of Rtg3 during fermentation to Rtg3-dependent recruitment of Nrg1 after the transition. Even as this dependence reversed, both factors remained necessary to establish the wild-type chromatin organization associated with each transcriptional state. Together, these findings show how one transcriptional complex can maintain activation of mitochondrial nucleoid genes while switching the regulation of cristae-organizing genes as cells transition to respiratory growth.

items.title: Sequence-to-function embeddings across individuals capture rare and common variant heritability
items.abstract: Statistical genetics learns how DNA shapes gene expression from variation across individuals, whereas sequence-to-function models learn from variation along the genome. Because sequence-to-function models map sequence to molecular readouts through deep architectures, their intermediate representations could offer function-informed descriptions of genetic variation. Whether these representations capture differences between individuals, however, is unknown. Here we introduce Embedding-based Heritability (EMBHER), a variance-component framework that estimates the expression heritability captured by these representations. Applied to Borzoi, embeddings recover much of the whole-blood heritability explained by genotypes and far exceed the model's final predictions. Deeper layers increasingly prioritize functional, evolutionarily constrained sequence while encoding less ancestry information than genotypes. Embeddings also explain more rare-variant heritability than genotypes, consistent with sharing information across variants too rare to estimate individually. EMBHER integrates sequence-to-function models with statistical genetics, a first step towards population-to-function models.

items.title: Lineage-specific LTR Retrotransposon Repertoires Engage OCT4-SOX2-SMARCA4 Chromatin Regulatory Architecture in Mouse and Human Pluripotent Stem Cells
items.abstract: Long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons contribute to regulatory sequences in mammalian genomes and provide binding sites for pluripotency-related transcription factors (TFs), such as POU5F1 (also called OCT4). SMARCA4 (also called BRG1), the ATPase catalytic subunit of BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF) chromatin-remodeling complexes, cooperates with pluripotency-related TFs and regulates chromatin accessibility. However, whether SMARCA4 preferentially occupies specific LTR subfamilies, whether it promotes chromatin accessibility at these elements, and how its occupancy relates to that of pluripotency-related TFs remains unclear. Here, we investigated the relationship between LTR retrotransposons and POU5F1-SOX2-SMARCA4 chromatin regulatory mechanisms in mouse and human pluripotent stem cells. Analysis of publicly available datasets revealed that SMARCA4 preferentially occupies specific LTR subfamilies, including RLTR13D6 and RLTR9E, in mouse embryonic stem cells. These LTRs exhibited accessible chromatin and active histone modifications, and were co-occupied by POU5F1 and SOX2. SMARCA4 depletion was associated with reduced chromatin accessibility and POU5F1/SOX2 occupancy at these LTRs, whereas POU5F1 depletion reduced both SMARCA4 occupancy and chromatin accessibility, suggesting cooperative binding. Taxonomic classification showed that most SMARCA4-bound LTRs belong to evolutionary young, rodent-specific families. Human pluripotent cells were also analyzed for the binding of POU5F1, SOX2, and SMARCA4, which revealed that a similar POU5F1-SOX2-SMARCA4 architecture engages primate-specific LTR families distinct from mouse LTRs. Our findings suggest that lineage-specific LTR repertoires can participate in a shared architecture of pluripotency TFs and chromatin remodeling factor. The association of evolutionarily distinct LTR repertoires with POU5F1/SOX2 and SMARCA4 in mouse and human pluripotent stem cells raises the possibility that non-orthologous, lineage-specific transposable elements were incorporated independently into similar regulatory architectures during mammalian evolution, generating lineage-specific cis-regulatory networks.

items.title: Genomic variation of Dutch traditional cattle breeds captured in a Dutch cattle pangenome
items.abstract: Traditional livestock breeds are reservoirs of genetic variation lost elsewhere by selection for productivity, yet are rarely represented in reference genome resources. Traditional cattle (Bos taurus) in the Netherlands are severely endangered, with some populations having declined by up to 95 % between 2020 and 2026. We generated 12 assemblies from seven traditional Dutch breeds and combined them with a Holstein Friesian assembly and the Hereford cattle reference to build the first Dutch cattle pangenome (2 881 293 997 bp), a graph containing 193.4 Mb of sequence absent from the international reference. More than 80 % of this sequence was breed private, and this fraction rose with variant size to 99 % for segments of at least one kilobase. Genotyping 54 short-read sequenced animals of these Dutch breeds against the graph recovered 55 865 structural variants and resolved four genetic clusters. The Groningen White Headed was the most differentiated breed while carrying the lowest nucleotide diversity, whereas the recently derived Improved Red and Deep Red remained close to their Meuse-Rhine-Yssel progenitor. Holstein Friesian formed no cluster of its own and contributed the least amount of novel sequence, a reflection of its historical use in upgrading traditional breeds. Ten structural variants located within genes were fixed within a single breed and ranked among the most breed-differentiated of all 55 865 SVs by VST , including a 174 bp deletion in KIT in the Dutch Belted. Pangenomes recover breed-defining variation that linear references cannot represent, supporting conservation and selection in traditional cattle.

items.title: Structural and functional reference maps of transcriptional enhancers in the developing human cortex
items.abstract: Non-coding regulatory variation is the major driver of human phenotypic diversity, yet maps of cis-regulatory elements (CREs) and their variability across developmental cell types remain limited. Here, we integrated single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from 54 mid-gestation human prenatal cortical donors to generate a CRE atlas comprising 1,165,697 candidate CREs across 104,266 cortical nuclei. Chromatin-state annotation classified 1.5% of CREs as bivalent promoters, 0.3% as active promoters, 39.8% as active distal enhancers, 1.3% as CTCF-associated insulators but 57.1% remain unresolved. Overlap with an external enhancer assay dataset showed that many unresolved CREs, nevertheless, exhibit regulatory activity; thus, current chromatin signatures underestimate the functional regulatory landscape. Pseudo-bulk analysis across major cortical lineages revealed that the prenatal cortical regulome is dominated by lineage-restricted CREs, with only a small core shared across all lineages. Restricted CREs were enriched for unresolved elements, intermediate-sharing classes were enhancer-dominant, and broadly shared CREs showed the strongest promoter-proximal and bivalent contribution. Lineage-selective transcription factor (TF) sequence grammar analyses identified progenitor-associated homeodomain programs and neuronal basic helix-loop-helix signatures, together with representative candidate regulators such as SOX10, NFIA, EMX2, DLX1, ARX, and RFX3. Across donors, developmental time, and sex, prenatal cortical CREs segregated into a stable versus variable regulatory compartments. Broadly, recurrent and developmentally persistent CREs had greater activity, on average, and greater enrichment for promoter-associated states, whereas donor-restricted and temporally restricted CREs had lower activity and were enriched for unresolved and enhancer-like elements. Sex-biased CREs were rare but highly specific: female-biased CREs were predominantly X-linked, broadly shared, and developmentally persistent, whereas male-biased CREs were more numerous, less resolved, and more restricted across lineage and developmental contexts. Together, these results define the prenatal cortical regulatory landscape at single-cell resolution, revealing a small, stable, promoter-rich core and a larger variable, enhancer- and unresolved-rich compartment in which lineage diversification is driven primarily by selective deployment of distal regulatory elements.

items.title: Heterogeneous Effects Across Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) Driver Mutations Challenges a Unified Model of CHIP
items.abstract: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is an age-associated expansion of hematopoietic stem cells harboring somatic mutations in the absence of overt malignancy. CHIP driver genes impart divergent effects on many biological processes, yet the mechanisms underlying these gene-specific effects, particularly in non-hematologic disease contexts, remain poorly understood. We analyzed 466 samples from the Multi-Ancestry Genomics, Epigenomics, and Transcriptomics of Alzheimer's Disease dataset, and identified function-specific differences between CHIP categorizations. Uniquely, DNMT3A CHIP was associated with global hypomethylation, STAG2 CHIP increased mutation burden, HSC differentiation CHIP strongly triggered adaptive immune response, and proliferative signaling CHIP induced coagulation and cell adhesion. These divergent functions differentially modulate inflammatory pathways and suggest investigating CHIP's downstream effects through a driver gene function-based approach rather than treating CHIP as a single entity. Our multi-omics analyses provide such a framework to improve mechanistic interpretation of conflicting relationships between CHIP and diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

items.title: scOnion: Cross-Modal Concordance-Aware Joint Analysis of Cells and Features in Single-Cell Multiomic Data
items.abstract: Single-cell multiomic assays jointly profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same cells, enabling direct analysis of cross-layer coordination. However, agreement between modalities varies across cells, and existing integration methods often emphasize shared structure, potentially averaging away cell-specific cross-modal discordance that carries biological signal. Here we present scOnion, a concordance-aware computational framework that quantifies cross-modality agreement and propagates this information into downstream analyses. Starting from paired low-rank representations obtained by spectral integration, scOnion computes per-cell concordance scores, a concordance-aware joint cell embedding, and an induced cross-modal feature embedding. The cell embedding preserves structure strongly represented in either modality, improving cell-type and state resolution, while the feature embedding scores candidate regulatory element(rE)-to-gene (rE2G) pairs. Across immune, neural, and developmental functional genomic datasets, scOnion's concordance patterns are reproducible and cell-resolved, with low-concordance cells enriched for modality-specific structure. scOnion also prioritizes candidate rE2G pairs, including distal links, with stronger support from external Hi-C contacts and fine-mapped eQTL data than the baseline linkage methods. In a B-cell fate bifurcation study, scOnion reveals remodeling of concordance and rE2G coupling during lineage commitment. scOnion embeds ~70,000 cells and computes rE2G links on CPU in 30 minutes, extends naturally to other multiomic assays such as CITE-seq, and is available as open-source software.

items.title: Population genomics of the Anopheles farauti complex reveals a distinct regime of malaria vector evolution in the southwest Pacific
items.corresponding_institution: School of the Environment, The University of Queensland, St Lucia, Queensland, Australia
items.abstract: Abstract: The southwest Pacific has one of the highest per-capita malaria burdens outside Africa, yet how its malaria mosquitoes evolve is largely unknown. In African vectors, insecticide resistance evolves rapidly in large, connected populations carrying abundant standing variation. Southwest Pacific vectors show little to no biochemical resistance despite decades of insecticide-based control. We analyse 495 genomes from six taxa of the Anopheles farauti complex, which includes the region's major vectors. The complex radiated rapidly in the late Pleistocene concomitant to the peopling of Near Oceania. Thereafter, post-glacial sea-level rise and climate change fragmented its populations into recently colonised island isolates. Successive environmental and colonisation bottlenecks left a legacy of extraordinary inbreeding, most marked in island populations of the coastal specialist An. farauti sensu stricto, where sustained low effective population size has allowed deleterious alleles to be purged effectively; the inland generalists An. hinesorum and An. oreios retain more variation. After five decades of chemical control we recover a single resistance sweep, at Gste2, alongside recent selection at species-specific chemosensory gene repertoires. Severe inbreeding and the loss of standing variation have not prevented ecological success, challenging assumptions about how much variation and connectivity a vector population needs to thrive. This work establishes the first genomic foundation for this major vector system of endemic species through a biogeographically diverse region of the world.

items.title: Transcription starting inside human introns is widespread but mostly yields short-lived RNA
items.abstract: Background: Thousands of annotated long non-coding RNAs lie inside introns of protein-coding genes, on the host's strand, but whether they are independent genes or pieces of host transcripts is usually unknown. An independent gene needs its own start site. Results: We mapped transcription starts inside introns, using nascent capped RNA from two human cell lines. The approach detected the start sites of 94% of clearly expressed protein-coding genes nested in introns and confirmed 1,346 and 3,061 intronic start sites, almost all unannotated. Most are cell-type-specific, carrying active chromatin marks and motifs of the cell's key transcription factors. Many initiate as strongly as the hosts' alternative promoters but rarely sustain transcription: after a synchronised restart of transcription, their nascent RNA fades within a few kilobases, their short transcripts are partly degraded by the nuclear exosome, and the sequence downstream rarely has the early splice-donor site that protects promoter transcripts. Per initiation event, they leave about as little stable RNA as start sites between genes, so host transcription does not explain their low output. Expressed intronic RNAs on the host's strand more often lack their own start site than those on the opposite strand. Conclusions: Transcription starting inside human introns is widespread but mostly yields short-lived RNA. Many intronic long non-coding RNAs on the host's strand are therefore likely to be pieces of host transcripts rather than independent genes, which matters for their annotation. All intronic start sites in both cell lines, with every measure used here, are provided as a resource.

items.title: No evidence of genome-wide selection against sensetranscription starts in human introns
items.abstract: RNA polymerase II often starts transcription inside genes, usually at elements that initiate in both directions. An intragenic start pointing in the gene's direction (a sense start) makes RNA that passes the gene's splice sites and polyadenylation signals and may interfere with the gene. Introns may therefore have lost sequences that start sense transcription. In PRO-cap data from K562 and HCT116 cells, the sense start at intronic elements, measured against the antisense start, is a fifth to a third weaker than at intergenic elements of similar read depth. Sequence models that have never seen an element's chromosome predict 30-42% of this bias from local DNA, except models trained on K562 applied to HCT116. However, introns as a whole show little or no depletion of predicted sense starts, and among 76,215 human genomes, variants predicted to create sense starts are not kept rarer than those creating antisense starts. In both cell lines, and in K562 GRO-cap data, strong measured start sites are rarer on the gene strand, mainly near the 5'' end of active genes. Thus, weaker sense starts appear to be a feature of individual active elements, partly predictable from their sequence, and we find no sign that selection has removed such sequences from introns.

items.title: Alternative splicing edits intrinsically disordered regions across human protein isoforms
items.abstract: Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) lack a stable three-dimensional structure, yet they mediate many of the interactions and regulatory functions of proteins. Alternative splicing produces multiple protein isoforms from a single gene, and because individual exons can encode all or part of an IDR, splicing has the potential to add, remove or reshape disordered regions. However, it remains unclear whether splicing preferentially acts on disordered sequence in all kinds of proteins, how it changes an IDR from one isoform to another, and how this relationship arose during evolution. Here, we map predicted disorder onto the coding exons and genomic codons of human protein isoforms, which allows any two isoforms of a gene to be compared directly, and analyze this map across protein classes and families. We find that alternatively spliced exons are more disordered than constitutive exons in every class of protein, from transcription factors to metabolic enzymes, and that splicing usually changes IDRs at their ends, adding or removing disordered segments as modular units rather than cutting through them. The disordered sequence that splicing varies is compositionally distinct from the disorder that all isoforms share. Notably, the apparent loss of disorder over gene evolution reflects differences between protein families rather than change within them, whereas exons whose splice sites are conserved in few mammals encode more disorder than the other exons of the same gene, with a composition resembling that of young genes. Our results suggest that alternative splicing treats intrinsic disorder as a modular, evolvable layer of protein architecture, and that exons with poorly conserved splice sites may be one route by which disordered sequence enters proteins.

items.title: Clonal landscape of human nephrons
items.abstract: The nephron is a highly compartmentalized structure, where distinct patterns of somatic mosaicism may be established and contribute to altered kidney functions with aging. Here we show extensive remodeling of aged nephrons by mosaic clones using integrated sequencing of >1,000 microdissected samples collected from anatomically distinct nephron segments. Striking differences were observed across segments. Proximal tubules exhibited markedly higher mutation burdens with mutational signatures characteristic of clear cell renal cell carcinoma and larger clonal expansion than other segments. Cancer-related mutations were observed only infrequently and largely limited to proximal tubules, while copy number abnormalities were quite common, most frequently involving chromosomes 18, 10, 7, X, 22, 3 and 9, in a segment-specific manner. Clone size appears to depend more on cell turnover than on driver events. Particularly, in collecting ducts, numerous clones independently acquiring chromosome 18 loss evolved over years and ultimately replaced 15-47% of collecting duct cells in aged donors despite minimal increase in their clone size, likely reflecting strong fitness advantage of chromosome 18-deficient clones under slow tissue turnover. Chromosome 18-deficient cells significantly correlated with fibrosis and showed reduced expression of chromosome 18 genes, including those involved in sodium handling (NEDD4L) and TGF-{beta} signaling (SMAD2/4/7). In line with this, GSEA of chromosome 18-deficient cells revealed enhanced hallmark pathways overlapping those associated with acute kidney injury that are related to TGF-{beta} signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and inflammatory responses. These findings illustrate how nephrons are remodeled with aging, providing insights into the role of somatic remodelling in altered kidney structures and functions with aging.

items.title: Functional interrogation of osteoarthritis-associated regulatory variants and effector genes.
items.abstract: Background: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci associated with osteoarthritis (OA); however, the regulatory variants and effector genes underlying most associations remain unresolved. Results: We used complementary functional genomic approaches in chondrocytes to resolve prioritized OA risk loci. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) in primary human chondrocytes identified allele-specific regulatory activity at variants across multiple loci, two of which were independently validated using low-throughput reporter assays. In parallel, integration of OA GWAS signals with chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac CUT&Tag, and chromatin conformation data prioritised candidate regulatory elements for CRISPR based perturbation. CRISPR activation and interference supported functional regulatory relationships between OA risk regions and Pappalysin 1 (PAPPA) and Sprouty RTK signaling antagonist 4 (SPRY4) as target genes. At the 9q33 locus, multiple independent lines of evidence converged on rs1895062, which resides in an accessible region that loops to the PAPPA promoter. The OA risk G allele at rs1895062 results in higher regulatory activity by MPRA and low throughput reporter assay. Activation of this region by CRISPR increases PAPPA gene expression and induces widespread transcriptional changes involving extracellular matrix remodelling and other OA-relevant pathways. Conclusion: Integrating genetic association, genomic and epigenomic data, and functional perturbation in disease-relevant cells can resolve the regulatory mechanisms underlying OA risk loci. Using this multi-faceted approach, we provide convergent functional evidence for rs1895062 as a likely causal variant that controls PAPPA gene expression and OA risk.

items.title: Differential gene expression profiling of lumbar disc degeneration in the RuDDS cohort
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Cytology and Genetics, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
items.abstract: Lumbar disc degeneration disease (LDDD) is a major structural cause of low back pain, one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, and has no disease-modifying treatment. We performed RNA sequencing of 72 intraoperative intervertebral disc samples from the Russian disc degeneration study (RuDDS) cohort, comparing severe (Pfirrmann grades IV-V) with moderate (grade III) degeneration. We identified 731 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 347 upregulated and 384 downregulated in severely degenerated discs) in the 57 samples that passed quality control. Upregulated DEGs were enriched for extracellular matrix organisation, ossification, and TGF-beta; and Hippo signalling, whereas downregulated DEGs were enriched for immune and inflammatory processes. We identified five differentially active transcription factors, including the TGF-beta; effectors SMAD3 and SMAD4 and the osteogenic regulator DLX5. Of the five, only DLX5 was also a DEG. DEGs were enriched for LDDD-associated genes from Open Targets (odds ratio = 1.68, P = 3.37 * 10-6). Connectivity mapping against the LINCS L1000 database showed that histone deacetylase inhibitors and glucocorticoids reverse the signature of severe degeneration. Together, these results point to TGF-beta-driven fibrotic and osteogenic remodelling as the dominant transcriptional feature of severe disc degeneration, and prioritise candidate genes and compounds for functional validation.

items.title: XenoType: Decoding cellular identity in breast cancer histology through molecular supervision
items.abstract: Characterizing the cellular composition of the tumor microenvironment from histological images is fundamental to understanding cancer biology and informing treatment decisions. Deep learning has enabled automated nuclear detection and classification from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images, yet cell classifiers remain largely confined to broad morphological categories owing to a reliance on manual annotations. Recent efforts have used spatial molecular measurements to supervise histological classification, but these approaches often require separate tissue sections or produce altered H&E staining, and the resulting cell-type annotations depend on subjective choices such as marker selection and clustering parameters. Here we develop XenoType, a framework that classifies cells into seven molecularly informed categories directly from routine histology, trained using paired same-section Xenium spatial transcriptomics. Cell-type annotations are reconciled from four single-cell RNA-sequencing references, reducing dependence on marker choices. Across eight held-out breast tissue sections, XenoType outperformed commonly used CellViT++ retrained on the same molecular annotations under both four-class (macro-F1: 0.703 vs. 0.569) and seven-class (macro-F1: 0.571 vs. 0.403) taxonomies, with the largest gains for myoepithelial (F1: 0.175 to 0.572) and endothelial cells (F1: 0.395 to 0.682). Molecular measurements are required only during training; at inference, XenoType uses the H&E image alone. Model-reference agreement increased consistently with annotation confidence, and XenoType generalized to an independently profiled breast tissue section from a different spatial transcriptomics platform, supporting scalable cell-type mapping from routine histology without per-specimen molecular profiling.

items.title: A pangenomic approach identifies new structural variants associated with gene expression in the CARTaGENE cohort
items.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are major contributors to the genetic diversity of human populations. While many small variants have been associated with human traits and diseases, the challenge to genotype SVs using short-read DNA sequencing and a linear reference genome has made association testing with SVs more difficult. To address these limitations and investigate the associations of SVs with complex human traits, we used PanGenie, a pangenome-based short-read genotyper, together with the second release of the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium (HPRC) pangenome to genotype 645,680 SVs in 2,173 participants from the CARTaGENE cohort. Through conditional eQTL analyses that account for associations attributable to known variation identified using a standard approach based on the GRCh38 reference genome, we identified 103 independent SV-eGene associations involving 99 unique SVs (SV-eQTLs). Of these associations, 41 replicated in the 1000 Genomes Project cohort (same direction of effect, nominal P-value 0.8) with small genetic variants (SNPs and indels) that belong to Open Targets fine-mapping credible sets, suggesting that these SVs are candidate causal variants for associations identified by genome-wide association studies. Our results highlight new opportunities offered by pangenome methods to more comprehensively integrate SVs into the study of human phenotypic variation.

items.title: Evaluating the Generalizability of Machine-Learning-Guided Directed Evolution Across Protein Fitness Landscapes
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Drug Discovery, Medical Faculty, Leipzig University
items.abstract: Machine-learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) prioritizes promising protein variants for experimental testing, but performance depends on campaign design. We present MLDEx, a systematic benchmark of 557,143 simulated campaigns across 16 protein fitness landscapes, covering 28 representations, eight regressors, three acquisition rules, four initial training-set sizes, and four batch sizes. Going beyond previous benchmarks, MLDEx jointly evaluates these design choices and tests whether recommended configurations generalize to unseen protein landscapes. With small initial sets, ML guidance required 2.2-2.8 times fewer assays than random screening for comparable success, but this advantage diminished with larger sets. At 200 total assays, zero-shot screening achieved 56.2% success versus 44.6% for MLDE, with similar performance at larger budgets. Representation-regressor rankings varied substantially between landscapes: configurations selected on 15 landscapes performed 13.3 percentage points worse on the held-out landscape. MLDEx identifies broadly applicable campaign-design principles but cautions against transferring model rankings to new proteins.

items.title: MEAM-OWL for browser-based analysis of motif enrichment and associations with gene expression
items.abstract: Motivation: Identifying functional regulatory motifs (such as cis-regulatory elements) remains challenging because conventional motif enrichment relies on binary comparisons between target and background sequences, overlooking quantitative relationships between motif copy number and gene expression or other quantitative traits. Existing tools for such analysis require specific and inconsistent input formats, incompatible with a streamlined workflow. Results: We present MEAM-OWL (Motif Enrichment Analysis Modules on the Web, Lite) to overcome those issues. As well as standard target-versus-background enrichment, MEAM-OWL can evaluate motif enrichment on the basis of either expression-ranked lists or Pearson correlation tests between motif counts and expression levels. These analyses can be preceded by sequence extraction and ingestion from genome and genome annotation files, and can be followed by annotation of detected motifs with known cis-elements from public databases. In pearl millet under dehydration, consistent with previous findings, MEAM-OWL detected the positive correlation between gene induction levels and the copy numbers of the drought-responsive ABRE (abscisic acid response element)-related motifs in their promoters. Furthermore, MEAM-OWL uncovered the correlations between the copy numbers of the VIP1-binding element in the promoters of Arabidopsis thaliana and the expression changes of mechanical stress-responsive genes across lines with perturbed expression of the transcription factor VIP1 and its homologs, as well as its enrichment that could be detected by a conventional tool. These results demonstrate that integrating quantitative expression-motif correlations can promote discoveries of biologically meaningful regulatory relationships and seamlessly connect them to hypothesis building and wet-lab validation. Availability and implementation: Source code and documentation are available at https://github.com/tsugama-eng/meam-owl. The archived v1.0.1 release is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24264754.

items.title: Phirefly: hierarchical quantum haplotype phasing at the chromosome scale
items.corresponding_institution: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard University
items.abstract: Motivation: Read-based phasing links alleles on the same homologous haplotype. It plays a critical role in long-read variant calling and variant analysis. Many phasing algorithms have been developed. This includes QHap, the only quantum-inspired algorithm for read-based phasing. QHap does not run on quantum hardware due to the scale of the practical problems. Results: We developed Phirefly, the first practical quantum algorithm for read-based phasing with the key phasing step executed on quantum hardware. Phirefly uses a CPU-based algorithm to identify small disjoint groups of SNPs linked by strong, consistent read support. These groups are called phaselets and are easy to phase. To phase across phaselets, which is harder due to weak or conflicting read support, Phirefly locks the relative SNP phases within each phaselet and applies a quantum algorithm, effectively treating each phaselet as one heterozygous variant. Phirefly runs on physical quantum computers from D-Wave and IBM, as well as with a quantum-inspired classical solver using CPU or GPU. It achieves broadly comparable accuracy to QHap and mainstream phasing algorithms on HG002 datasets. Availability and implementation: https://github.com/wangyf1125/Phirefly

items.title: A method to disentangle enhancer-gene interactions from latent factors in single-cell multi-omics data
items.corresponding_institution: Boston Children's Hospital & Harvard Medical School
items.abstract: Mapping regulatory elements to their target genes in the cell types relevant to disease is essential for interpreting non-coding variants identified by genome-wide association studies. Single-cell multiome data, which simultaneously measure accessible chromatin and gene expression per cell, allow such peak-gene links to be inferred within individual cell types. However, shared technical and biological variation across genes and peaks, such as cell cycle, cell quality, and inter-sample differences, creates spurious links, while including sample covariates to control for this variation inadvertently removes true genotype-driven links. To address this trade-off, we developed CREMAP (Covariance-of-Residuals-based Enhancer-gene Mapping), a statistical method that estimates shared variation as latent factors from the data and adjusts for them before testing each peak-gene pair. Using CRISPRi perturbation experiments and fine-mapped eQTLs as validation benchmarks, we demonstrate that CREMAP improves the accuracy of inferred peak-gene links compared with existing methods across two cell lines and 13 cell types from human bone marrow, brain, and kidney. In kidney proximal tubule cells, CREMAP retains eQTL-supported and allele-specific links that standard approaches miss when samples are included as covariates. Furthermore, its latent factors capture previously unrecognized global signatures, including a tubular injury program. CREMAP thus enables accurate cell-type-specific peak-gene mapping from single-cell multiome data while preserving genuine genetic regulatory effects.

items.title: ChronoClone links temporal clonal behavior to lineage output and mutation responses
items.abstract: Distinct stem cell clones can yield similar lineage outputs via different developmental trajectories or dynamics and respond differently to perturbation. Here, we introduce ChronoClone, an unsupervised method that groups single-cell clones by time-resolved cell-state composition into metaclones. Benchmarked against simulated ground-truth scenarios, ChronoClone demonstrates high noise tolerance compared to existing methods. Applied to an adult mouse hematopoietic lineage-tracing dataset, ChronoClone showed that clones producing the same lineage mature at different speeds, a difference the original study did not examine. Furthermore, using WT metaclones as a baseline reference for Dnmt3a- and Npm1c-mutant sister-clones, ChronoClone uncovered hidden, clone-specific mutation responses including slowed maturation and lineage composition shifts. By connecting temporal dynamics, perturbation responses, and ancestral molecular states, ChronoClone adds temporal cell-state dynamics into clonal analysis.

items.title: Does embedding impact classification performance ? A small sample perspective
items.corresponding_institution: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology
items.abstract: Deep learning (DL) methods can address many challenges posed by high-dimensional and sparse microbiome data. In this study we applied and compared deep (DNN) and shallow (SNN) feedforward neural networks combined with five dimensionality-reduction techniques: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Autoencoder based Embeddings (AE), and convolutional layers (Conv). To establish baseline classification performance, the XGBoost was used, as it represents a robust machine learning based classifier with a relatively low number of hyperparameters. The task was to classify effective microorganism (EM) treatments based on intestine bacterial family abundance in common carp. In particular, the experiment involved 25 ponds that were divided into experimental groups. In each pond, the intestinal microbiome of five individuals was determined by sequencing two hypervariable regions of the gene encoding the 16s rRNA gene sequencing. The sequence reads were processed by QIIME2 and taxonomically annotated to the SILVA database, what resulted in 126 annotated families that were used as features in all downstream analyses. Abundance tables from 125 samples, transformed using the Centered Log-Ratio (CLR) method, were used to evaluate ten dimensionality-reduction and Deep learning configurations considering five-, three-, and two-classification scenarios. The DL models were optimized using cross-validation. To combat the overfitting that was present due to sparsity and small sample size, dropout and kernel regularization were implemented. During testing autoencoder embeddings achieved the highest classification accuracy (0.84), exceeding the XGBoost baseline (0.64), while embedding based on convolutional layers significantly reduced performance (0.44). PCA and SVD transformations showed comparable results (0.65), whereas NMF often failed to converge, likely due to incompatibility with CLR-transformed data. Best classification results were obtained for models that implemented AE embedding, it is most likely caused by their ability to capture non-linear patterns in the data. All models showed stable training behavior, with loss functions consistently decreasing across epochs. The SNN models were markedly less computationally intensive, than DNN. AE and NMF based embeddings were the most resource hungry (Wall Clock Time and RAM). Our results show (1): SNN architectures performed slightly worse than DNN, due to the fact of lesser informative capacity of the models. (2): Dimensionality reduction impacts model performance, though not always positively. (3) EM supplementation causes significant changes in microbiome that can be captured by DL architectures. Future work will include feature-importance analysis, integration of environmental and host metadata, exploration of larger datasets and more advanced architectures. As well as validation of model quality on simulated datasets. Overall, these results indicate that DNN architectures combined with AE embeddings have potential to be used as high accuracy classification tools. Those tools when combined with feature importance can help researchers to understand changes made by EM supplementation in a microbial community.

items.title: CyteArc: in-place analysis and reuse of remote atlases at 100-million-cell scale
items.abstract: Public repositories hold hundreds of millions of single-cell profiles, yet analyzing them still requires downloading full files. We present CyteArc, a framework that analyzes remote atlases in place, scaling to nearly 100 million cells on standard CPUs faster than benchmarked workflows, with the lowest memory from 10 million cells upward. Without copying counts, CyteArc integrates millions of cells across studies using 1% to 4% of the disk space of other tools. CyteArc saves every step with full provenance, keeping analyses reproducible and letting researchers branch without rerunning upstream stages. Because those saved steps stay linked, completed cloud atlases act as live references, annotating new datasets without exporting reference files. Using CyteBase, an open cloud repository of over 160 million single-cell and spatial profiles in CyteArc format, we screen over 30 million blood cells across cohorts in minutes and identify rare circulating progenitors whose expansion tracks COVID-19 severity.

items.title: BRIDGE: inter-tissue imputation with contrastive learning improves recovery of donor-specific gene expression
items.abstract: Multi-tissue transcriptome resources are central to understanding tissue-specific regulation and inter-individual variation. Realistically, most tissues are measured in only a subset of donors, especially for less accessible tissues such as brain and heart. Accurately imputing gene expression values for such tissues, while accounting for individual heterogeneity, remains a daunting challenge. Here, we present BRIDGE (Body-wide Representation via Inter-tissue Decoding of Gene Expression), a lightweight framework that imputes donor-specific and tissue-specific expression measures using contrastive learning. When tested on real-world expression data from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) consortium, BRIDGE recovered donor-specific variation more accurately than existing state-of-the-art methods while improving overall accuracy, with the largest advantage found in the most inaccessible tissues. We provide the BRIDGE-imputed completed GTEx v11 donor x tissue xgene expression tensor as a resource to the broader research community.

items.title: GASTON-VI efficiently quantifies spatial axes and molecular gradients from multi-sample, multi-modal spatial-omics data
items.abstract: Many tissues exhibit an underlying spatial axis along which fundamental biological processes occur due to continuous spatial gradients of cell type and molecular state. Modern spatial-omics technologies measure molecular features (e.g. gene/protein expression) at 100,000s-1,000,000s of locations within a two-dimensional (2-D) tissue slice, with large-scale atlases profiling multiple tissue slices of the same organ type across different individuals and biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). However, existing computational methods for identifying spatial molecular gradients are limited to small spatial transcriptomics datasets (1000s of cells) of a single tissue slice, while methods for integrating multiple samples do not explicitly model spatial axes nor spatial molecular gradients along such axes. Here, we present GASTON-VI, a variational inference (VI)-based deep learning model which efficiently learns an underlying spatial axis and spatial molecular gradients along this axis from multi-sample, multi-condition spatial-omics data of any molecular modality (e.g. transcriptomics, proteomics). GASTON-VI jointly learns (1) a spatial coordinate (the "isodepth") for each individual tissue slice and (2) 1-D spatial modality functions that describe molecular gradients along the isodepth for tissues of the same biological condition, while utilizing a latent variable model to account for batch effects. Further, GASTON-VI implements a statistical test for identifying molecules with differential spatial gradients across biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). On spatial transcriptomics and proteomics data from the intestine, tonsil, and liver, we show that GASTON-VI recovers spatial axes and molecular gradients along these axes more accurately and efficiently than existing methods. In particular, applied to large-scale spatial transcriptomics and proteomics atlases, GASTON-VI reveals differential spatial gradients of gene expression along the portal vein-central vein axis in fibrotic livers, and differential spatial gradients of protein abundance along the muscularis-lumen axis across different regions of the intestine. Software availability: GASTON-VI is available at https://github.com/chitra-lab/GASTON-VI.

items.title: BRISANCE: A GPU-Accelerated Pipeline for Somatic Short-Variant Detection in Whole-Genome Sequencing Data
items.abstract: Post-sequencing computational processing of tumor-normal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) remains computationally intensive and can delay somatic variant detection in clinical and translational workflows. We developed and evaluated BRISANCE, a graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated pipeline based on NVIDIA Parabricks for detecting somatic single-nucleotide variants and short insertions/deletions, using matched tumor-normal WGS data from the Cancer Genome in a Bottle HG008 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma model. Concordance with the DRAGEN-derived comparator call set was assessed using allele-level variant-set comparison, RTG Tools haplotype-aware benchmarking, and IGV manual review of four literature-reported HG008-T sample loci. Runtime was measured in two analyses: a fixed CPU-GPU comparison and GPU-scaling experiments. At the analyzed whole-genome call-set level, the PASS-filtered, positive-TLOD Parabricks set and the PASS-filtered DRAGEN set contained 17,134 and 16,885 variants, respectively, sharing 14,430 variants and yielding an intersection-over-union overlap of 73.66%. Shared fractions were 76.09% for single-nucleotide variants and 69.06% for insertions/deletions. Using the DRAGEN-derived call set as a comparator rather than a validated truth set, RTG score-based filtering increased comparator-based precision from 0.8375 to 0.9110 and F-measure from 0.8569 to 0.8821. Qualitative IGV review showed consistent read-level support at the four selected HG008-T loci. In the fixed CPU-GPU comparison using the HG008 tumor-normal dataset, the summed runtime of the evaluated preprocessing and somatic variant-calling components was 10.6 hours for the GPU-accelerated workflow versus 219.4 hours for the CPU-based workflow, corresponding to a 95.1% reduction and a 20.6-fold speedup under the evaluated conditions. In GPU-scaling experiments, alignment/preprocessing reached its shortest runtimes with 6-8 GPUs, whereas MutectCaller reached its shortest runtime with 2-3 GPUs, depending on CPU-thread configuration. Full-input Nextflow execution reproduced the historical CHROM/POS/REF/ALT record set, and a configuration-based interface was developed for user-defined analyses.

items.title: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
items.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. This spillover is niche-dependent and can therefore confound downstream analyses that rely on niche-specific differential expression. True spillover cannot be directly quantified in experimental ST data, so existing correction methods infer contamination indirectly from transcript positions or expression structure. Here we introduce SYNDRI, a post-segmentation correction method that frames spillover detection as a supervised, gene-level classification task. We develop SYNDRI-SIM to generate labeled training data by simulating spillover between spatially mapped scRNA-seq profiles. SYNDRI uses a transformer to predict gene-level spillover probabilities conditioned on each cell's expression, identity, and local neighborhood, without requiring transcript-level coordinates or deconvolution. On held-out simulated data, SYNDRI achieves an AUPRC of 0.86, compared with 0.64 for the next-best method. Across MERFISH, CosMx, and Xenium datasets, SYNDRI achieves the highest aggregate performance across metrics of cell-type separation, reference similarity, and preservation of within-cell-type heterogeneity. In a CosMx lung cancer dataset, SYNDRI removes nearly all potentially contaminating tumor and macrophage markers from differential expression between tumor-associated and stromal fibroblasts while retaining native fibroblast markers. These results demonstrate the utility of learning from simulated spillover to improve the interpretation of spatial gene expression.

items.title: SPECTRE: A versatile data framework for integrating spectral, environmental, and ecophysiological trait data
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Biology, University of Toronto, Mississauga, ON, Canada L5L1C6
items.abstract: With the increasing availability of large datasets and the growing importance of artificial intelligence (AI), robust and sustainable data management systems have become essential for plant and ecosystem research. In particular, the integration of heterogeneous spectral data with plant functional traits and environmental measurements from multiple sensors poses a major challenge, requiring significant time investment and long-term planning. Here, we present SPECTRE (Spectral, Trait, and Remote-sensing Ecophysiology data framework), a versatile data framework based on simple, open data formats that addresses the need of many research groups for a standardized organization of heterogeneous datasets, facilitating their integration and joint analysis without relying on proprietary software or external service providers. SPECTRE integrates a wide range of datasets linking spectral measurements to plant traits, including LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery, chlorophyll fluorescence, geospatial data, soil moisture, climate variables, and ecophysiological traits, organized into three main categories: (i) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-acquired data, (ii) ground-based trait measurements, and (iii) environmental data. All datasets are stored using a standardized folder structure and converted to comma-separated values (CSV) format. A unified primary key enables consistent linking of spectral signatures to functional traits across datasets by species and site, facilitating trait-based analyses, data framework extension, and long-term usability. The widespread use of lookup tables reduces data redundancy and facilitates the integration of data with different naming conventions, while the use of Markdown for metadata and documentation ensures easy access to information without relying on complex or proprietary formats, simplifying documentation creation and maintenance. Overall, SPECTRE offers a simple, transparent, and scalable solution that can be readily adopted by plant ecophysiological laboratories, facilitating future AI-driven trait prediction analyses.

items.title: Random-walk-based Probabilistic Microglia Morphology Reconstruction in 2D and 3D from Confocal Microscopy Images
items.corresponding_institution: University of Rochester, Department of  Biostatistics & Computational Biology
items.abstract: Reconstructing individual microglia from confocal images is challenging when fine processes have weak fluorescence or neighboring cells form connected structures. Inspired by Grady's random-walker framework, we propose a soma-guided probabilistic method for three-dimensional microglial reconstruction and cell-of-origin assignment. Signal-weighted random walks quantify voxel connectivity to each soma by the probability of reaching that soma before background or another soma. A path-length adjustment reduces the penalty on distal processes. Adjusted scores are compared across somata to assign voxels, subject to score and image-intensity thresholds. We assess process recovery and cell assignment separately using exact three-dimensional matching to manual tracings. In a P28 single-cell example, the reconstruction covered 83.98% of traced voxels within the analyzed region. For a connected cell pair in sample 12hrMD82, coverage was 71.86% and 82.31%, with a pooled incorrect-assignment rate of 4.61% among detected traced voxels. Local analyses were also combined to produce an overview of 13 cell reconstructions in the same sample. We additionally provide a two-dimensional version that tolerates short signal gaps in maximum-intensity projections. These initial examples demonstrate the potential of soma-specific connectivity for microglial reconstruction.

items.title: RNAhub2: prefiltering and compression enable scalable structure-based RNA discovery
items.abstract: RNAhub is an established web server for structure-agnostic RNA homology search that builds multiple sequence alignments with nhmmer and performs downstream structural covariation analysis with R-scape and CaCoFold. RNAhub is efficiently applied to smaller genomes, including viruses, bacteria, and fungi. However, searches against large eukaryotic genomes remain computationally expensive, and genome storage requirements currently limit its taxonomic coverage, thereby reducing the opportunities to identify novel structural RNAs. Here, we present RNAhub2 which introduces three key advances to address those limitations: (i) query-adapted pre-filtering that creates a reduced query specific search database prior to iterative alignment construction; (ii) parallelized genome-level searches with job resumption; (iii) Nucleotide Archival Format (NAF) compression of genomes, reducing storage by approximately 4.2 fold and enabling the addition of nearly 5,000 species across major eukaryotic kingdoms within the original storage quota without increasing computation time. These combined updates yield significantly improved runtimes and comparable or stronger covariation signal. RNAhub2 is now scalable for eukaryotic comparative RNA searches without sacrificing sensitivity. The web server is freely available at https://rnahub.org.

items.title: Functional cooperation, adaptation and synchronization of subcellular processes in cellular neighborhoods as inferred from spatial transcriptomics
items.corresponding_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
items.abstract: Tissue-level functions emerge from pathway activities distributed across neighboring cells. Yet analyses of spatial transcriptomics mostly focus on cell type composition or signaling through ligand-receptor pairs, leaving spatial relationships between effector processes undescribed. We inferred networks of functionally interacting subcellular processes (SCPs) that are independent of shared gene products and lie beyond sibling relationships defined in parent-child hierarchies. Using those networks for the analysis of published spatial transcriptomics datasets from human kidney biopsies, we identified functionally related SCP activities between a tissue spot and its neighbors. Identified pairs of adjacent SCPs indicate functional cooperation, e.g. basement membrane assembly and cell-matrix adhesion, functional adaption, e.g. complement synthesis and inhibition, and functional synchronization, e.g. folate cycle and cobalamin metabolism or pre-mRNA splicing and nuclear mRNA export. Two independent null models, shuffling of SCP labels within the network and shuffling of spots on the tissue slice, distinguish pairs that are functionally non-random and pairs that are additionally enriched within the immediate neighborhood, separating local from tissue-wide coordination. Our results suggest that tissue physiology reflects not only cell type composition but also functional coordination between neighboring regions.

items.title: Niche-FATE: niche-aware inference of cell-state transitions from spatiotemporal data
items.corresponding_institution: Danish Research Institute of Translational Neuroscience (DANDRITE), Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine, Aarhus University, Aarhus, Denmark
items.abstract: Cell-state transitions depend on intrinsic transcriptional programmes and local signals. Existing spatiotemporal mapping methods largely match cells by expression or position, not by received signals. Here we introduce Niche-FATE, an optimal transport framework integrating gene expression, spatial neighbourhoods and inferred ligand-receptor signalling to estimate transition probabilities and prioritise fate-associated signals. In simulations with changing tissue organisation, Niche-FATE improved fate inference and recovery of known fate-determining signals (mean AUPRC of 0.46 versus 0.29 for the best-performing alternative). In digit tip regeneration, Niche-FATE reduced inconsistent regenerative-to-scar transition assignments from 28% without niche information to 7%. Niche-FATE also improved developmental transition inference in mouse organogenesis. In two mouse models of Alzheimer's disease, Niche-FATE linked predicted microglial transitions to local signalling, recovered amyloid plaque associations without plaque-location input and predicted transitions from disease-associated towards homeostatic-like states. Niche-FATE enables researchers to resolve divergent cellular outcomes and investigate their associated signalling environments.

items.title: An interpretable framework for decoding transcriptomic foundation models
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Computer Science, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA; Department of Biomedical Engineering, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA
items.abstract: Transcriptomic foundation models are pretrained on millions of single-cell profiles, but what their hidden states encode, and whether it holds on targeted spatial panels, is uncertain. We present interpreTFM, a layer-resolved framework that extracts frozen activations from scGPT, Geneformer, and C2S-scale, decomposes each evaluated layer with a sparse autoencoder (SAE), and evaluates the resulting features against raw hidden dimensions, an untrained SAE of the same width, and single genes, holding out either gene-token rows or whole genes. Concept-associated features are then projected to cells for spatial niche discovery and interface analysis. We applied the framework to a CosMx lung-cancer section (81,236 cells, 960 genes) and a Xenium renal-cell-carcinoma section (465,220 cells, 399 model-compatible genes), screening 29 model-layer combinations per dataset. On held-out observations of known genes, sparse features marked 262--593 biological concepts per analysis layer, against 0--70 for raw hidden dimensions and 0--249 for the untrained SAE; on genes held out during feature selection, concept F1 was 0.01--0.12 for every representation and lowest for sparse features, so a feature's concept label reflects the genes it detects, and randomly re-initialized models scored the same. A linear readout of the hidden states recovered the concept membership of unseen genes (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.66--0.75, versus 0.59--0.61 for co-expression and cell-type profiles, and chance level for randomly re-initialized scGPT and Geneformer), so this information is learned and distributed across dimensions. At the cell level, sparse features were about twice as population-specific as raw hidden dimensions and approached single marker genes, and this held in four further CosMx donors. In the analyzed CosMx section, niches built from sparse features agreed with author cell types more closely than label-composition and expression-only niches and converged across models; in the further donors their concept-level definition recurred, whereas their composition did not. In the single Xenium section, three of five niches per model (lymphoid, tumor/myeloid, tumor/vascular) were shared across models and also emerged from measured expression alone. A macrophage's sparse profile predicted the myeloid composition of its neighborhood about as well as the full gene panel, also in three further donors. Within model niches, ligand--receptor co-localization recurred directionally across CosMx donors and placed CCL19--CCR7 in the Xenium lymphoid niche, whereas the models' own interface calls, under a local, stratified null with a threshold calibrated on contact-free fields, were at chance level in CosMx and tracked transcript spillover in Xenium. interpreTFM thus provides held-out tests that separate gene detection from concept generalization, and features that make cells and niches comparable across models and patients while carrying the information of the measured panel. Source code is available at \href{https://github.com/OliiverHu/interpreTFM}{github.com/OliiverHu/interpreTFM}.

items.title: HGCF/LGCF classification from (Mavrich and Hatfull, 2017) is explained by heterogeneity in pairwise ANI rather than by intrinsic evolutionary modes
items.corresponding_institution: Univ. Grenoble Alpes, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK, 38000 Grenoble, France
items.abstract: Mavrich and Hatfull proposed that phages could be separated into two broad evolutionary modes (high gene-content flux or HGCF; and low gene-content flux or LGCF) according to the rate at which their gene content changes relative to nucleotide sequence divergence. In their analysis, HGCF phages appeared to gain and lose genes substantially faster relative to genome divergence than LGCF phages and were particularly associated with temperate phages. However, as the analysis represents a comparison between two phage genomes, the difference between the two groups identified in their study (HGCF/LGCF) should not be interpreted as a property of either phage (such as their lifestyle) as they suggest. Instead, it should be explained by a property inherent to the comparison such as the organization of the shared regions between both genomes. Indeed, the two groups identified in the original study reflect differences in the ANI (average nucleotide identity) and coverage of aligned regions between pairs of genomes and is independent from the gene-content similarity central to the original interpretation. More fundamentally, we show that the k-mer based genomic similarity used in the original study (namely Mash) is biased towards short regions of very high nucleotide identity, which exaggerates the differences described previously. This is particularly important for phage genomes which are often mosaic: closely related regions can alternate with more divergent or unrelated regions, and the number, length and identity of these regions can differ markedly between genome pairs.

items.title: Tuning evolutionary information in MSAs shapes protein generation and folding
items.abstract: Protein multiple sequence alignments are widely regarded as fixed artifacts of homologue retrieval. An alignment's row composition shapes the evolutionary context that is supplied to a protein model. In this study, we tested whether tuning row composition would steer protein generation and structure prediction outcomes. We tuned lower-tail alignment information by controlling row selection within a reference protein-projected coordinate frame. We paired each information-targeted alignment with a matched-depth random-row control alignment. Across a cohort of 45 diverse proteins, row coherence among the retained homologues is predictive of structural confidence readouts and generated sequence novelty. The strongest row-coherence states occur near an empirical lower-tail information reference point of 1 bit/site. Below this reference point, generated de novo sequences demonstrate more eager exploration, higher decoder uncertainty, and reduced structural confidence at mutated positions. Across an independent structure-prediction benchmark, controlling the fraction of low-information positions demonstrated that intermediate fractions of low-information positions were associated with improved structure prediction within a confidence-gated subset. These findings evince that evolutionary information in protein alignments can be tuned to shape protein generation and structure prediction results.

items.title: A modular decomposition framework of the CHO transcriptome reveals lineage, genomic, and process-responsive cell states
items.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) transcriptomic studies have generated diverse datasets across parental lineages, cell-line development histories, and culture conditions. However, the transcriptional programs underlying this heterogeneity remain difficult to compare and interpret across studies. Here, we asked whether heterogeneous CHO transcriptomes could be organized into reproducible and biologically interpretable transcriptional modules. To address this, we assembled a discovery compendium of 778 quality-controlled RNA-seq samples spanning multiple parental lineages, engineered cell backgrounds, culture conditions, and perturbations, and applied robust multi-run independent component analysis, resulting in 105 independently modulated gene sets, termed iModulons. To accommodate mammalian regulatory and genomic complexity, we interpreted these modules by integrating gene function, activity-metadata associations, promoter motifs, genomic localization, and RNA-biotype composition. The iModulons captured lineage-associated variation, chromosomal enrichment, and responses to temperature downshift and antiviral stimulation, together with an ATF4-associated amino-acid-stress program. Projection of 377 independent samples onto the discovery-derived iModulons reproduced selected lineage- and process-associated activity patterns and captured a glutamine-deprivation response not represented in the discovery compendium, supporting the transferability of these modules across datasets. When the compendium was expanded to 1,155 samples and ICA was repeated de novo, 89 of the 105 discovery iModulons were preserved among 148 expanded modules, while an additional CHO-DXB11-associated transcriptional pattern emerged. To our knowledge, this study represents the first application of the iModulon framework to a mammalian cell system, establishing a transferable and expandable set of transcriptional coordinates for comparing CHO cell states across heterogeneous datasets and prioritizing programs relevant to cell-line and bioprocess engineering.

items.title: VenusPheno: Transfer-Guided Task Grouping for Multi-Task Bacterial Phenotype Prediction
items.abstract: Understanding how genomic information gives rise to bacterial phenotypes is a fundamental problem in biology. Genome-level prediction requires models that integrate information from thousands of proteins, while related phenotypes may share genomic signals. However, not all phenotype tasks benefit from being learned together, and suitable task groups can be difficult to define from biological knowledge alone. We present VenusPheno, a framework that combines multiple-instance learning over pretrained ProtT5 protein embeddings with transfer-guided multi-task learning. An attention-based Set Transformer aggregates the proteins in each genome into a genome-level representation. We evaluate VenusPheno on 14 binary phenotype tasks from 12,178 bacterial genomes using genus-disjoint splits. Under single-task training, VenusPheno outperforms computational, conventional machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines in terms of mean balanced accuracy. We then use leave-one-task-out analysis to estimate directed transfer relationship between phenotypes, revealing both beneficial and detrimental interactions. Grouping tasks based on these transfer relationships further improves mean balanced accuracy over independent training and joint training of all tasks. Although inferred without biological priors, the resulting groups are consistent with biologically plausible relationships among phenotypes. VenusPheno therefore combines accurate phenotype prediction with a data-driven strategy for determining which tasks should be learned together. The PyTorch implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/YJinling/VenusPheno.

items.title: A noise-corrected metric for evaluating spatial transcriptomics predicted from histology
items.corresponding_institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
items.abstract: Deep learning methods that predict spatial transcriptomics from histology offer scalable molecular profiling of clinical cohorts. However, conventional correlation metrics overstate prediction quality across whole sections by crediting models for recognizing broad tissue regions, and understate fine-scale prediction quality because sampling noise dominates sparse RNA counts. To resolve this, we introduce the reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) metric. RSC randomly splits RNA counts into two halves to separate reproducible signal from sampling noise across spatial scales and within tissue regions or cell classes. Across 12 spot-level and three single-cell methods, RSC revealed that most models capture broad tissue patterns but largely miss differences between neighboring spots or cells, which whole-section correlation overlooks. Within malignant cells, RSC distinguished methods that genuinely capture part of the cell-to-cell heterogeneity from those whose scores across all cells were inflated by cell-type composition.
