items.corresponding_institution: Service de Neurophysiologie Clinique, CHU de Bordeaux, Bordeaux, France; Univ. Bordeaux, CNRS, Institut des Maladies Neurodegeneratives, UMR 5293, Bordeaux, Fra
items.abstract: Adaptive deep brain stimulation could make the treatment of essential tremor more responsive to patients' needs, delivering stimulation when tremor-provoking movements occur rather than continuously, thereby potentially reducing habituation-related loss of efficacy and stimulation-induced adverse effects. Its success, however, depends on neural control signals that remain measurable and meaningful long after surgery, at home rather than in the laboratory, and while stimulation is running. Thalamic local field potentials offer such candidate signals, yet they have largely been characterised intraoperatively or in the early postoperative period, under supervised conditions that reveal little about their behaviour in daily life. We therefore followed nine patients with essential tremor implanted with a sensing-enabled neurostimulator targeting the ventral intermediate nucleus and posterior subthalamic area, combining in-clinic recordings three and six months after surgery with weekly, patient-performed home recordings. We extracted 13 spectral features encompassing canonical and tremor-frequency band power, aperiodic spectral properties and periodic beta activity, and evaluated their agreement between home and clinic recordings, between-session reliability and movement-related modulation across recording settings and stimulation states. Oscillatory features did not differ systematically between home and clinic, whereas the aperiodic background was consistently steeper at home and poorly reproducible. Periodic beta measures emerged as the most robust candidates: with stimulation off, their clinic-home reliability approached that observed between the two clinic visits, and a postural task suppressed beta activity across recording settings, an effect carried by the periodic component rather than by the aperiodic background. Stimulation, however, reduced the reliability of beta measures and markedly attenuated their movement-related modulation, precisely under the conditions in which an adaptive controller would need to operate. Within the limits of this small cohort, thalamic beta activity therefore appears unlikely to serve as a stand-alone control signal for adaptive stimulation in essential tremor, highlighting the potential need for complementary cortical or peripheral inputs.

items.title: Single-Cell Gene Expression Heritability Informed by Genotype x Cell-Context Interactions
items.corresponding_institution: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School
items.abstract: Most signals from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of complex traits implicate noncoding variants with putative gene regulatory effects. However, currently identified regulatory variants, particularly expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), explain only a small fraction of GWAS associations. Moreover, GWAS loci are enriched near evolutionarily constrained genes, whereas constrained genes are depleted of detectable eQTLs, suggesting that weak or context-specific regulatory mechanisms may contribute substantially to disease risk but remain poorly captured by existing approaches. Here, we introduce scHINT (single-cell gene expression Heritability estimation with genotype x context INTeraction), a computationally efficient framework for quantifying cell-level expression heritability and context-dependent genetic regulation from large-scale single-cell data. Applying scHINT to human brain single-nucleus RNA-seq data, we found that genotype-by-cell-state heritability was widespread across brain cell types and, on average, exceeded main genetic heritability, indicating that context-dependent genetic effects explain a substantial fraction of heritable expression variation. GxCell-State heritability was enriched among low-frequency variants and constrained genes, and showed stronger enrichment for functional gene sets and disease heritability than main genetic effects. Using a novel GxCell-State TWAS framework, we identified 68% more disease-risk genes and recapitulated rare-variant burden-test gene TREM2, which was missed by state-agnostic TWAS. In blood, we observed the same direction of enrichment for GxCell-State heritability at constrained genes, but weaker than in brain, suggesting that cell-state-dependent regulation at constrained genes may be more prominent in brain. Finally, extending scHINT to perturbation screens revealed substantial perturbation-by-cell-state effects, highlighting broad context dependence in transcriptional responses.

items.title: Automatic cerebral angiographic perfusion analysis
items.abstract: Purpose: To automate anatomical localization for angiographic perfusion and evaluate agreement with manual processing between biplane projections in a held-out external cohort. Methods: Separate anteroposterior (AP) and lateral projection hemisphere and internal carotid artery (ICA) models used DeepLabv3+ with ResNet50 encoders. Development used patient-separated training, validation, and testing. External patients were excluded from fitting and model selection. Automated pipeline and manual-pipeline perfusion shared downstream calculations. Eligible acquisitions contained at least 7 seconds of data after bolus arrival. Segmentation metrics and Bland-Altman analyses evaluated mean transit time (MTT) and time to maximum of the residue function (Tmax). Results: External segmentation testing included 353 runs from 73 patients. Patient-mean hemisphere Dice was 0.959 (95% CI, 0.952-0.965) in AP and 0.965 (0.960-0.969) in lateral views while ICA Dice was 0.635 (0.617-0.650) and 0.558 (0.534-0.579). Manually processed perfusion comparisons included 165 external runs from 52 patients. Mean absolute differences (95% CI) were 0.39 (0.31-0.47) and 0.32 (0.25-0.40) seconds for AP and lateral MTT, and 0.23 (0.15-0.35) and 0.31 (0.17-0.51) seconds for Tmax. Among 220 external cohort biplane pairs from 61 patients, mean absolute differences were 0.48 seconds (95% CI, 0.42-0.53) for MTT and 0.53 seconds (0.35-0.75) for Tmax. Repeated-measures mean biases (95% CI) were -0.07 (-0.19 to 0.05) and 0.16 seconds (-0.08 to 0.40), with 95% limits of agreement of -1.38 to 1.24 and -2.65 to 2.97 seconds respectively. Conclusion: Our automated perfusion pipeline showed favorable agreement with manually processed results in the external validation cohort. Independently processed biplane views had small average bias.

items.title: Continuous at-home wearables and machine learning sensitively track function and progression in pediatric and adult Friedreich's ataxia
items.abstract: Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) is the most common hereditary ataxia, characterized by progressive cerebellar and sensory ataxia, proprioceptive loss, and upper motor neuron involvement, with onset typically in childhood. Current outcome measures used in clinical trials are limited by rater subjectivity, coarse scoring, infrequent in-person assessments, and inability to assess behavior continuously in naturalistic settings. We tested whether submovement-based measures derived from accelerometers worn continuously at home could sensitively capture motor impairment and disease progression in FRDA across a range of ages and disease severity. 95 participants (57 FRDA, 38 controls; age 2-75) wore GENEActiv wrist and ankle sensors for one week per timepoint; 60 completed two or more timepoints spanning up to 2.2 years. 85 movement features were extracted including submovement kinematics and activity intensity. The FRDA cohort included ambulatory and non-ambulatory participants spanning early, mid, and late stages of disease. Five machine-learned composite models were evaluated, including FRDA-specific models, and models previously trained on other populations. Sensor measures were evaluated for relationships with clinician-rated and patient-reported measures, reliability, and sensitivity to progression. Ankle sensor measures demonstrated strong cross-sectional correlations with Friedreich's Ataxia-Functional Disability Staging (|r| = 0.66-0.87), Modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale total (|r| = 0.53-0.73), Friedreich's Ataxia-Activities of Daily Living (|r| = 0.58-0.74), and Friedreich's Ataxia-Health Index total (|r| = 0.43-0.57), with high within-week reliability (ICC = 0.89-0.96) and large differences between FRDA and control groups (|e.s.| = 2.0-2.6). FRDA-specific composite outcomes showed significant longitudinal sensitivity to disease progression (|MSDR| = 0.67-0.89), whereas patient global impression of change did not capture progression. At-home ankle accelerometer data yield reliable, ecologically valid measures reflecting clinician-rated and patient-reported outcomes, and capture disease progression in FRDA. These results support remote wearables as sensitive digital outcome measures for FRDA clinical trials and disease monitoring.

items.title: Non-Blood Liquid Biopsy of Nipple Discharge to Decode Tumor-Derived CNV Signatures for Breast Cancer Detection and Prognostication
items.corresponding_institution: National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College
items.abstract: Accurate, noninvasive diagnosis of malignant nipple discharge remains a longstanding clinical challenge. This study evaluated somatic copy-number variations (CNVs) in nipple discharge DNA (ndDNA) as high-fidelity diagnostic biomarkers and explored their cellular origins and shedding mechanisms. We derived a 20-feature CNV panel from large-scale genomic datasets and validated its diagnostic potential. Integrative single-cell analysis of 50 patients revealed that these features predominantly arose in ancestral states across molecular subtypes and exhibited functionally relevant co-occurrence patterns. In clinical cohorts, ndDNA-based detection achieved 74.4% sensitivity and 94.4% specificity (AUC = 0.863), significantly outperforming plasma cell-free DNA (AUC = 0.517; p < 0.0001). Paired single-cell RNA sequencing confirmed high concordance between ndDNA profiles and malignant epithelial cells. High-fidelity epithelial subclusters displayed active estrogen signaling and distinct immune interactions, and a derived Fidelity Score independently predicted favorable prognosis in two external survival cohorts. Our findings establish nipple discharge as a tumor-proximal liquid biopsy that preserves early tumor genomic signatures with minimal dilution, advancing noninvasive diagnostic and prognostic strategies.

items.title: The cellular neighbourhoods of adult gliomas and their clinical associations
items.corresponding_institution: Division of AI in Oncology, German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany
items.abstract: Glial tumours are the most common primary malignant brain tumours in adults and comprise molecularly and histologically distinct entities with diverse outcomes. Despite this diversity, they arise within a shared anatomical environment, suggesting that common organisational principles may shape tumour heterogeneity. However, how cellular states are organised across gliomas and whether this organisation relates to clinical outcomes remains unclear. To that end, we generated a single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas of 2.6 million cells from 275 patients spanning IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, IDH-mutant and chromosome 1p/19q codeleted oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant astrocytoma and ependymoma. Across diagnoses, we show how heterogeneous tumour cell states are spatially organised into recurrent neighbourhoods with distinct immune and glial composition, which in turn assemble into a higher-order architecture. Among these cellular neighbourhoods, some, such as the astrocyte-like (AC-like), are conserved across entities, whereas others segregate by clinicopathological parameters. AI-powered histopathology further reveals selective association of neighbourhoods within histological clusters, providing a link between molecular spatial organisation to routine H&E morphology. In astrocytoma, neighbourhood abundance is associated with patient survival independently of WHO grade, with AC-like enrichment linked to favourable outcomes. Same-cell high-plex spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed protein imaging in an independent astrocytoma cohort validated these neighbourhoods and further confirmed enrichment of oligodendrocytes within the TBI neighbourhood. Collectively, our findings reveal that glial tumours are spatially encoded through recurrent multicellular neighbourhoods across different molecular entities, showing clinical relevance beyond conventional histology and providing a foundation for analogous investigation across cancer types.

items.title: Dependence-aware aggregation maps shared genetic architecture across cardiovascular traits
items.corresponding_institution: Division of Cardiovascular Sciences, School of Medical Sciences, Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health, The University of Manchester, Manchester, UK
items.abstract: Background Shared genetic effects are pervasive across clinically related cardiovascular diseases and can expose biology that crosses diagnostic boundaries, but correlation between related phenotypes (shared patients, risk factors, overlapping definitions) makes naive cross-trait recurrence hard to interpret because evidence is counted repeatedly. We asked which genes carry coordinated positive association across a complete cardiovascular panel beyond the recurrence expected from trait dependence. Methods We developed the Cross-Trait Aggregation Score (CTAS), a per-gene statistic applied to MAGMA gene-level association across 16 Pan-UK Biobank cardiovascular traits. Panel dependence was estimated as a transformed rank-correlation matrix; each gene's 16-trait profile was decorrelated by ZCA-cor whitening to remove the expected correlation; and CTAS combined the magnitude and effective breadth of positive residual evidence across the whitened coordinates. The statistic was calibrated against an empirical null of 10 simulated profiles, with genome-wide Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control, after which significant genes were merged into loci and characterised by clinical-family composition, expression colocalisation, comparison with prior multi-trait studies and FinnGen. Results CTAS prioritised 223 genes at 91 loci (q<0.05), with nested sets of 99 genes at 46 loci (q<0.01) and 38 genes at 21 loci (q<0.001); membership was identical across independent null simulations. The loci formed an overlapping multi-family continuum rather than discrete disease classes: 88% spanned at least two clinical families and the fraction spanning four or more increased from 21% to 43% across the nested sets. Expression colocalisation supported 31 of 91 loci (31 of 87 evaluable). Literature convergence with four prior multi-trait studies covered 58 of 91 loci and 17 of the 21 most stringent loci. In FinnGen, the proportion of CTAS genes with external support across at least three of six clinical families of cardiovascular endpoints increased across the nested sets, from 49% at q<0.05 to 57% at q<0.01 and 61% at q<0.001, against 6% of background genes. Conclusions CTAS evaluates a complete correlated trait panel in one calibrated test per gene, discounting the recurrence expected from trait correlation. In cardiovascular disease, it prioritised genes and loci with multi-family, independently supported evidence, providing a focused starting point for mechanistic and translational follow-up.
